- Tests: `test_ha_card_convert.py` at 16 scenarios (state labels, the area's photograph and its compact default, alert icons) and `test_ha_card_host_runtime.py` at 4 — the new one asserts the `hass` shape is complete enough to INDEX INTO, which is the failure that produced a blank card with no error anywhere.

## grid_options, and cards that show only what they were asked for (v2.197.0)

- **`grid_options` now decides a card's size, in every stack.** Reported as the thing most noticed: the property was in the YAML and did nothing, so every card in a stack was the same size. Home Assistant honours these only in a SECTIONS view and ignores them inside a stack — here they are honoured everywhere, because the complaint is the same either way: without them there is no way to say the flow diagram deserves twice the room of the gauge beneath it.
- **Every stack is now the SAME twelve-column grid**, and the direction only picks the default span — vertical takes all twelve, horizontal an equal share, `grid` a share of its `columns`. That unification is what lets a card's own `grid_options` mean the same thing wherever it sits; two different grids would have made the number mean two different things. `rows` maps to `--nc-row: 56px`, HA's own section row height, so a value copied out of a dashboard is the height it was there. `columns: full` and `rows: auto` mean "the stack's default", so a config that never mentions them lays out exactly as before.
- **The area card stopped inventing controls.** It put a row of toggles on every card, so a board showed six switches under "Main House" that the YAML never mentioned — the same card in HA from the same config showed none. Controls are opt-in there (`features`), and a card that invents them is worse than one that lacks them: it is the difference between reading a config and guessing at one.
- **Hosted cards say states properly too.** `hass.formatEntityState` returned the raw state, so a mushroom lock card printed `unlocked` where HA prints `Unlocked`. The label table is a small duplicate of the server's AND HAS TO BE: `hass.states` must carry the raw state, because cards branch on `'on'` and `'unlocked'` to decide what to draw. Only the display is translated.
- **The grid's limits were judgement, not technical, and were too tight.** `grid-auto-rows` takes any length and `repeat(N, …)` any count. Row height was 80–600 and columns ≤24 on the reasoning "surely nobody wants more" — the same reasoning that made the row height a menu of seven. Now `ROW_MIN/ROW_MAX = 40/2000` and `COLUMN_MAX = 48`, named constants the tests read rather than repeat, guarding what actually breaks (0 columns divides by zero, a 5px row makes every span meaningless) rather than taste. Raising the column cap is safe for existing boards — spans are counts of columns and the board's count is a separate setting, so nothing rescales until somebody changes it, which the editor now warns about in place.
- Tests: `test_ha_card_convert.py` at 18 scenarios, including clamping and nonsense in `grid_options`, the size riding on hosted cards and nested stacks as well as leaves, and the area card showing nothing it was not asked for.

## No taste limits, locks by consent, and a web tile (v2.198.0)

- **The grid's limits are runaway guards now, not judgement.** Asked whether a high column count or a low row height costs anything: it does not. A wide grid is O(N) track sizing per layout pass, unmeasurable next to drawing the tiles; a short row creates more implicit rows, and an implicit row with nothing in it costs nothing to lay out. The work in a board is proportional to the number of TILES, and that does not change when the grid under them gets finer. So `ROW_MIN/ROW_MAX = 1/10000` and `COLUMN_MAX = 1000`, and the only thing they now prevent is a mis-keyed 100000 turning into a hundred thousand grid tracks on a Raspberry Pi.
- **Locks are a decision, not a refusal.** `panel_allow_unsafe_controls` adds `lock`, `cover`, `garage` and `valve` to what a tap may operate. `alarm_control_panel` is NOT covered and is not a toggle away — disarming an alarm is the one control here whose failure mode is not "somebody opened a door they could have opened anyway". The important half is that every surface asks the same question: `home_board.toggle_domains()` is the single answer, and the entity tile, the native cards and the hosted-card service endpoint all call it. Two copies of that list is how a lock ends up working from one card and not another.
- **New `web` tile** — any address, in a frame. The most generic tile there is, which is the argument for it: nothing about a Home Assistant dashboard makes it the only page worth putting on a wall, and a bus timetable or a school lunch menu will never have a tile of its own. Options are url, reload interval, scroll and zoom. The zoom is a TRANSFORM rather than CSS `zoom` (Firefox does not apply that to frames), with inverse width/height so the page still fills the tile at any scale. The URL is checked for a scheme and nothing else: this is a frame in the household's own browser going where they typed, with no server fetch to protect and no token to leak, so a validator would only be inventing rules about which of their own pages they may look at.
- **Two pre-existing faults the work surfaced**, both in the settings registry's coverage audit: `ingest_sender_blocklist` was read and written all over `main.py` and `email_ingest.py` but was **never declared on the `Settings` model** — the audit had been failing on main and was right. And `panel_grid_columns`/`panel_grid_row_height`/`panel_tile_spans` became unreachable by name when pages took over, since the controls now bind to `page().columns` and friends; they carry `ui_marker` now, which is exactly the honest exception that field exists for.

## Visual card editors, the card's own (v2.199.0)

- **A custom card's own editor now runs here.** Every card worth configuring ships `static async getConfigElement()` in the bundle we already fetch — an ordinary Lit element that takes `hass` and `setConfig(config)` and fires `config-changed`. What stopped it working was never the editor: it was what editors are BUILT OUT OF, `<ha-form>` driven by Home Assistant selectors plus the entity and icon pickers, all of which live in HA's frontend bundle.
- **`static/ha_form.js` is those.** `ha-form`, `ha-selector`, `ha-entity-picker`, `ha-icon-picker`. The bet, stated plainly: a selector schema is a DECLARATION the same way a built-in card's config is — `{selector: {entity: {domain: 'light'}}}` says "an entity of this domain", not "draw this widget" — so honouring it is a real implementation rather than an impersonation, and it draws in the panel's own vocabulary.
- **Proven against the real thing.** mushroom 5.2.2's `mushroom-lock-card-editor`, untouched, mounts and draws **11 fields across six selector kinds** (entity, text, icon, select, boolean, ui_action) with a working entity picker.
- **An unknown selector is SHOWN, not dropped** — as an editable raw value with a line saying why. `ui_action`, `target`, whatever HA invents next: a form that silently omits the one option somebody opened it to change is worse than one that shows them JSON. Same rule as an unsupported card keeping its cell.
- **Built-in cards get editors too**, from schemas declared in `ha_card_convert._SCHEMAS` beside the builders that honour them — their real editors live inside HA's frontend and cannot be fetched, same wall as the cards. A test asserts **every field named in a schema is a key some builder actually reads**: a form offering an option the drawing ignores is a worse lie than no form.
- **The card picker reads `window.customCards`** — the registry every card bundle pushes itself onto as it loads, and the one HA's own picker reads. There is no server-side answer: a file's name does not tell you which elements it defines (`mushroom.js` defines about thirty). Bundles are loaded on demand when the picker opens, and one that fails to load cannot take the picker down with it.
- **YAML and the visual editor share one config**, converted on the SERVER (`POST /api/ha/card/config`, both directions). There is no YAML in the browser and adding one would be two implementations that have to agree about a format famous for surprises.
- **Also**: the 12-row cap on a tile's span is gone. Columns are bounded by the grid — a tile cannot be wider than the board — but rows are not, the grid grows downward, and 12 read as arbitrary at 240px a row and as broken at 20.
- Tests: `tests/test_ha_form_runtime.py` (4 scenarios) — a native schema drawing its declared fields with the config's values already in them, an edit emitting the whole object (what card editors listen for), the unknown-selector fallback carrying its value and explaining itself, and the schema-vs-builder coverage guard.

## Arranging the cards inside a tile (v2.200.0)

- **The same gesture as the board's, one level down.** A tile made of a stack of cards is a layout too, and the reason to drag it is the reason tiles got dragging: typing numbers into a list and scrolling up to see what happened is the long way round.
- **What moves is a PATH into the config tree.** The drawing is one HTML string, so there is no object on the page to point at — `0.1` is the second card of the first column, and `cardParent()` resolves it to the LIST the card sits in plus its index, because every edit here is a splice. Each cell carries its own `data-path`, threaded down through `drawCard` rather than looked up: a nested stack's children are two levels deep and nothing about a node says where it sits.
- **Reordering is confined to one stack.** Moving a card between columns changes which list it belongs to, which is a different edit — and doing it by accident mid-drag is how a layout comes apart under the hand.
- **The handles are markup, not an overlay**, for the same reason: anything positioned against a cell has to be inside it. Which means they must not be drawn when nobody is arranging, and a test asserts exactly that — handles on an idle board are handles on a wall.
- **Resizing writes `grid_options`**, so the drag and the YAML and the visual editor's size fields are all the same setting seen three ways. A card's columns are twelfths of ITS OWN STACK, not of the board, since that is the grid it is laid out on. The cell is restyled live and the config is only written when the numbers actually change — a round trip per pixel would be a save per pixel.
- Tests: `test_board_arrange_runtime.py` at 6 scenarios; the new one covers path resolution at both depths, a reorder taking, every cell carrying its address, and the handles being absent unless arranging.

## A card can be sized without sizing its neighbours (v2.201.0)

- **The resize was two-dimensional but not independent.** A grid row is as tall as its tallest cell, and cells stretched to fill it — so dragging one card taller dragged everything beside it to the same height. The sizes existed precisely to escape "every card in a stack is the same size", and the height half of them was still enforcing it.
- **A stack holding any sized card stops stretching** (`.nc-stack-grid.nc-free`); a stack nobody has sized keeps stretching, because ragged bottoms on a row nobody has touched read as a mistake rather than a choice. The switch is decided per stack while drawing, and applied to the live element for the whole drag — otherwise a card dragged SHORTER sits in a row still held open by a neighbour and nothing appears to move until the pointer comes up.
- **`rows` is now a `height`, not a `min-height`.** A minimum can only ever grow a card, so dragging the grip upwards did nothing and the card looked stuck. A card sized smaller than its contents clips, which is what asking for it means.
- Tests: `test_board_arrange_runtime.py` at 7 scenarios; the new one asserts the sized stack frees itself, the unsized one does not, and that exactly the sized card carries a height.

## Tile content became cards (v2.203.0)

- **The content a board shows used to be welded to the chrome around it.** A chores list existed only inside the tile called Chores — there was no way to put one anywhere else, or to put anything beside it. Splitting the two gives a **card** (content, nothing else) and a **tile** (a container with a grid, and optionally a heading over it).
- **There are two kinds of tile and they are the same tile.** A **built-in** tile is `{id, type: 'chores', config}` — exactly what every board has always stored — assembled at build time into a LOCKED container holding one card of that type, with the heading and the link out belonging to the tile. **Because the stored shape did not change, no board anywhere needed migrating and the surface a household already knows still works.** A **custom** tile is `{id, type: 'custom', config: {title, cards: [...]}}`: starts empty, takes any number of cards, lays them out on its own twelve columns. Blank title → a plain panel, which is what somebody wanting one surface under three cards is asking for.
- **One drawing per type, included twice.** `components/board_tile_body.html` is the board's tile body pulled out into a partial and included by both the built-in path and the custom path, with `t` rebound to the card. The options form went the same way (`components/board_options.html`, instance variable substituted at compile time). Two drawings of chores would have drifted apart inside a year.
- **`+ Add tile` adds a tile of whichever type you pick**: a built-in comes with its heading and its one card; Custom comes empty with an add-a-card control. `custom` joins the PAGELESS list — it summarises several pages, so there is no one page for it to open.
- **A built-in tile's card keeps the TILE's id** so every element id that predates cards still resolves; a custom tile's cards are namespaced by the tile (`mine-calendar`), because a card draws the tile body element ids and all and would otherwise collide with a same-typed tile. `drawnTiles()` is now every card in every tile — anything that mounts into the page (timeline, map canvas, hosted HA card) looks there.
- **`tile.data` still means what it meant.** A built-in tile having exactly one card is not an implementation detail, it is what a built-in tile IS, so everything that reasoned about `tile.data` before cards existed still reasons correctly.
- **Arranging works inside a custom tile**: drag to reorder, drag the corner to resize in twelfths, and ✎ opens the card's own settings in an **overlay over the board** — a layout is judged by looking at it, and scrolling to a list further down the page is the long way round that dragging replaced. `cardsOf()` reads order and size from the DRAFT while arranging so a drag shows its result immediately; content still comes from the server, because only the server can build it. Columns floor at 1, rows floor at 0 ("as tall as the content"), and a value at its default stops being stored.
- **A container cannot hold a container** — the markup that draws a card is the markup that draws a tile and cannot include itself, and a layout nested three deep is not read from across a room.
- **Reversed from v2.202.0**: the short-lived `group` tile (a container with an inherited person subject) is gone. It was a tile inside a tile — every cell redrew the full tile chrome — and it was built around an example rather than the ask. A designed **Person card** is the right home for that idea and is not built yet.
- Not yet: month/week/day views on the calendar card (the people filter it already has, under the card's gear); a compact-vs-full choice on the chores card; the Person card.
- **Groundwork (v2.203.2): the calendar page got a real-DOM test before anything moves.** Its month/week/day grid is due to become a component the board can mount as a card, the way `components/schedule_timeline.html` already serves both the Drives page and the drives tile — but the page is a 1700-line singleton (one `window.calendar`, one `window._agendaActive`, ~25 element ids read without a null check, a `tuneMonthDensity()` reaching for `.fc-daygrid-day-frame` with an unscoped `document.querySelector`). `test_calendar_render.py` pins what it does today: the grid mounts and the schedule reaches it, all four views are reachable, agenda is a PANEL that replaces the grid rather than a library view, the people legend is built from the schedule's own members, and `?view=` pins a view without writing to localStorage (shared across every card iframe on the origin). Assertions are on the event STORE, not the paint — jsdom measures everything as zero, so `dayMaxEvents` folds the month into a "+N more" popover and an empty grid is honest there.
- **Fix (v2.203.1), off a photograph of a real wall**: every mosaic, map and camera tile collapsed to nothing, and quiet tiles said so twice. Applying "a tile is a container of cards" literally put a grid and a flex cell between a built-in tile's content and the tile — and a mosaic, a map and a camera are laid out INTO their tile with `flex-1`, so two extra boxes meant zero pixels tall. Nothing threw; the tiles just went blank. A built-in tile now renders its card with **no grid, no cell, and a `display: contents` wrapper** — present for Alpine, absent from layout — which is byte-for-byte the DOM it had before cards existed. The empty message comes from the card body alone, since a tile's data IS its card's data. Both are pinned by real-DOM scenarios now.
- Tests: `test_board_cards.py` (11 scenarios — the built-in tile as a locked one-card container, `tile.data` still its own, rule 1 one level down, id collision, nesting, clamping, a card that throws), 3 new runtime scenarios in `test_board_arrange_runtime.py` (draft-drawn order and size, defaults not stored, the overlay opening on the tapped card), and a real-DOM scenario in `test_board_render.py` proving a custom tile's calendar card draws the calendar's own body at the right size.

## The calendar grid became a component (v2.204.0)

- **One calendar renderer in this app, not two.** FullCalendar's month/week/day grid moved out of the calendar page into `components/family_calendar.html` — the same move `components/schedule_timeline.html` made for the Drives timeline, and for the same reason: a board that needed a calendar would otherwise have grown a second, smaller one that drifts away from the real one over a year. A test asserts `new FullCalendar.Calendar` appears in exactly one file.
- **The library is lazy.** 282KB, injected on first MOUNT rather than by including the component. That is the performance requirement made structural: a board carrying an agenda-only calendar card downloads none of it, because the agenda is hand-drawn and needs none of it.
- **What deliberately did NOT move**: the agenda panel, the people legend, and the two modals. Those are the calendar PAGE's chrome. The component takes `onAgenda`, `onEventClick` and `onDatesSet` as optional callbacks and works with none of them — which is what lets a wall panel mount a grid where there is nothing to click through to. `headerToolbar: false` removes the view bar entirely, because a card pinned to one view does not want three buttons offering to un-pin it.
- **Mountable more than once.** State is per instance in a `Map` keyed by container id, and `tuneMonthDensity` measures `.fc-daygrid-day-frame` **inside its own element** — the page's version read it off the `document`, so a second calendar anywhere would have set its density from the first one's cells. Re-mounting the same container destroys the old instance, or a board redraw would leak a calendar per poll.
- **The page kept its own duplicate for one commit and it was a real bug**: `_postCalendarInit` still ran `render()`, a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` and a `ResizeObserver`, all of which the component now does — two of each per calendar, each firing the other's work. What remains of it is two lines of page chrome.
- `FamilyCalendar.pause(id, on)` is wired into the agenda toggle: the agenda hides the grid rather than destroying it, and a hidden calendar measures zero — a geometry the density tuner would otherwise act on.
- Tests: `test_calendar_render.py` at 6 scenarios, written BEFORE the extraction and unchanged by it — the grid mounts and the schedule reaches it, all four views are reachable, agenda is a panel that replaces the grid, the custom `eventContent` builder is still the one drawing (asserted via the event's LOCATION, which FullCalendar's own renderer knows nothing about), a forced `?view=` never writes to localStorage, and the structural claims above.
- Next: the calendar card itself — `view` and a show/hide toggle for the view selector — which deletes the board's separate agenda drawing.

## Blank means blank, and a tile can drop its panel (v2.204.1)

- **Two panels and two headings around one card is clutter, photographed off the wall**: a custom tile drawing a surface, a card drawing another inside it, the tile's title above and "A Home Assistant card" above that — over a card that already says what it is.
- **A card's heading is what you TYPED.** Blank draws nothing and takes no row. This splits two questions that had been one: `label` is what the editor calls a card in a list of five (always has an answer, since a list has to be navigable), `title` is what gets drawn on the wall. The board payload now carries both.
- **`bare` on a custom tile** removes the panel behind the cards, so they float on the board. Built-in tiles cannot: their single card wears no surface of its own — the tile IS the surface — so removing it would leave content on the wallpaper. Same rule as the untitled tile, one level out.
- Tests: 2 scenarios in `test_board_cards.py`, 2 real-DOM scenarios in `test_board_render.py` (an untitled card draws zero `.panel-label`s; a bare custom tile has no `panel-card` class while a built-in still does).

## The calendar card: month, week, day and agenda (v2.205.0)

- **The four views asked for, on a card**, and month/week/day are the calendar PAGE's own grid mounted from `components/family_calendar.html` — not a smaller copy. `view` now offers agenda, list, month, week and day; `view_selector` shows or hides FullCalendar's button bar, which is off by default because a card pinned to a view does not want three buttons offering to un-pin it.
- **Cost is paid per view, which was the requirement.** Agenda and list are drawn from the board payload — no library, no extra request, exactly as light as before. Month/week/day mount the component, which injects the 282KB library on first mount. A board with no grid card downloads none of it.
- **The events pipeline moved too.** `fetchCalEvents` — `api/schedule` into FullCalendar event objects, with participants, aliases, errands and unassigned handling — is now `FamilyCalendar.events()`. One pipeline, because the page's grid, the page's agenda and any card have to agree about what an event IS; three answers to that is three calendars disagreeing in front of the family. Host-specific parts are options and all are optional: `aliases`, `hidden` (the page's legend), `only` (a card pinned to one person), `onRoster` (so a host that draws a legend can). The page keeps a ten-line wrapper that passes its legend in.
- **`base` is an option, not a guess.** The old `pathname.endsWith('/')` heuristic resolves `api/schedule` to `/board/api/schedule` on `/board/hallway` — this app's one two-segment route — and under ingress a wrong guess climbs out of the add-on. The board passes its own `apiBase`.
- **A card's people filter is resolved server-side from ids to NAMES**, because the pipeline matches people by the name their calendar carries. Shipping the ids would have been a filter that silently never hit.
- Tests: `test_board_render.py` at 14 scenarios (a calendar card mounts a real grid, with its toolbar suppressed), `test_calendar_render.py` at 6 unchanged by any of it.
- Still on the list: the board's separate server-built agenda drawing, which the component's own agenda should replace; and the chores card's compact-vs-full view.

## The chores lane view got a test before it moves (v2.205.1)

- The chores kiosk's lane-per-person view is next to become a shared component, so a board card can offer a **full** view beside the existing compact leaderboard. Third page renderer this session to start serving two surfaces, and the first two taught the same lesson twice — the board tiles went blank on a real wall, and the calendar's `eventContent` could have been dropped without an assertion going red.
- `test_chores_lanes_render.py` pins the lane view as it stands: one lane per person with points in leaderboard order, each with its own balance and earned status; **the slicing is per lane and by member id** (a chore restricted to one child is not offered to another, a claimed chore appears only in the claimant's lane, an open one appears in every eligible lane); and the actions are the interactive half that a wall card will want switched off.
- The per-lane identity is the part most easily broken by componentising. There is no stored "current member" anywhere — every action passes the tapped lane's id — because two children at one wall panel are two lanes in use at once, and a single shared identity would have each claiming the other's chores. That failure is invisible to one person testing alone.
- Extraction shape, from reading it: the lane markup is pure Alpine with **no element ids and no `querySelector` anywhere**, driven by four arrays (`balances`, `chores`, `rewards`, `redemptions`) plus slicing helpers. So the shared contract is those four arrays and the helpers — the page fetches them, a card will get them in the board payload, and the markup does not change.

## The calendar page IS the calendar card (v2.206.0)

- **Parity, the thing the card was missing.** `components/family_calendar.html` now owns the WHOLE calendar surface — grid, hand-drawn agenda, people legend, details dialog, view selector — each an independent mount option. The calendar page collapsed from ~970 lines to ~400: one mount call with everything switched on (`toolbar`, `legend`, `details`, `agendaDays`, `onConfigure`), plus the one thing that stayed deliberately — the event-configuration EDITOR, which is admin chrome, is not on the panel/kiosk, and per the scope rule never becomes part of a card.
- **The view selector now includes Agenda everywhere.** Agenda is one of the component's four views, reached through the same `changeView` as the grids, so a card with `view_selector` on offers exactly what the page offers. The facade returned by `mount()` reports `view.type === 'agenda'` and hides whether a FullCalendar instance exists yet.
- **The cost model is structural**: the grid (and the 282KB library) is built the first time a grid VIEW is asked for, and never before. `?view=agenda` — the wall panel's normal morning — renders day cards with zero library. Switching to Month from the agenda toolbar lazy-loads it at that moment.
- **Per-instance everything**: hidden-legend set, aliases, roster, agenda anchor/days/sequence live on the instance, so two calendar cards on one board are two filters and two agendas. The details dialog and popover backdrop are emitted once per page by the include and shared.
- **Hooks are the page's memory, not the component's**: `onViewChange`/`onAgendaDays` fire and the PAGE decides about localStorage (URL-forced views still never write). `onConfigure` is how the editor button appears — no hook registered (kiosk, boards) means no button.
- Fixed on the way: the events pipeline referenced the page's `_calCarryParams` — on any board, a trip event in range would have thrown inside the events callback and blanked the grid. It is a `carryParams` option now.
- Board mounts pass `base`/`only`/`agendaDays` as data instead of an events closure. Still to flip (next): the board's `agenda`/`list` payload views — agenda should mount the component's agenda so the last second drawing dies; `list` stays a payload view (genuinely different, one line per event).
- Tests: `test_calendar_render.py` at 7 — the new parity scenario starts in `?view=agenda`, asserts the day cards draw and that tapping a row opens the details dialog; the other six survived the rewrite with probes retargeted to the component's DOM (`.cal-grid`/`.cal-agenda`/`.cal-legend`).

## One agenda, and boards that actually load (v2.207.0)

- **The last of the three agenda drawings is gone.** The calendar card's `agenda` view now mounts the component's own agenda — the same drawing the calendar page shows, fetched by the component itself. The builder returns mount config (`view`, `days`, `toolbar`, `only` as names); nothing rides in the board payload. Only `list` is still payload-built, because one line per event for a narrow tile is genuinely a different drawing, not a copy. The old server-drawn day cards, their markup, `agendaCols()` and `AGENDA_PER_DAY` are deleted.
- **What the day cards promised, the component agenda delivers**: a card per configured day whether or not anything is on it, and finished events greyed rather than dropped — the greying moved INTO the component, so the calendar page gained it too. The board's poll calls `FamilyCalendar.refresh(id)` on live mounts, since the payload no longer carries anything for them to redraw from. `calendar` joined `DRAWN_TILES`: a month grid drawn into a block-flow tile has no height to claim.
- **FIX, reported off a real wall: `/board/{slug}` never loaded its assets.** nav.html climbed for its links and `apiBase` climbed for fetches, but home.html's `<head>` loaded `static/...` bare — which on a two-segment route resolves to `/board/static/...` and 404s. **No stylesheet and no Alpine: a board opened directly was a page of raw, giant, unstyled markup.** Pre-existing since boards shipped (v2.188), invisible to every jsdom test because the harness strips script tags and injects Alpine from disk. The head now computes the same `_up` climb nav uses; the component's lazy library loader learned the same arithmetic.
- Also fixed: v2.206's export patch had silently no-opped (unconverted line endings, no assert), so `FamilyCalendar.closeEvent` — which the details dialog's close button calls — did not exist. The export now carries `closeEvent`, `setView` and `refresh`.
- Tests: the payload-agenda scenarios were rewritten to their new subjects (mount config resolution + everything the LIST inherits: whole day in order, past flags, trip-span exclusion, drivers named, needs-driver colour); a real-DOM scenario asserts the built-in calendar tile mounts the component agenda with a card per configured day and no view switcher. `test_day_of_traffic` fails near midnight on a clean tree too — time-of-day dependent, pre-existing, not this work.

## A board you can walk up to and edit (v2.208.0)

- **The editor opens pointed at the board being looked at.** `pageIndex` was never initialised from the URL slug, so `/board/kitchen` showed the kitchen while "Add tile" below it silently edited the home board — only `startArrange()` knew to sync. `loadSetup()` now resolves the slug to its index once the pages arrive.
- **"Open to edit ↗"** joined "Open as a panel ↗" under the editor: every other road to a custom board (the shelf, the panel link) carries `?panel=true`, which latches the whole tab into panel mode and hides every edit tool. The new link opens the board with `?panel=false` — the one thing that clears the latch — so arranging a board while standing in front of it is a click, not URL surgery.
- **The board's address is editable.** The `/board/<slug>` line in the editor is an input now (`setPageSlug`): lowercase, slug-safe, home reserved. The shelf's curated order stores boards as `board:<slug>` and `resolve_tabs` drops keys it does not recognise, so the rename REMAPS the shelf entry in the same keystroke — without that, renaming a board silently took it off a curated shelf.
- **Drives and Calendar wore the same icon (v2.311.0).** Byte for byte, and they sit next to each other on the shelf: two identical glyphs, two different pages, nothing in the row to say which one you were about to open. Drives takes the **truck** — a vehicle is what a drive is, and it is the only vehicle in this icon family, so it is also the only shape that could not be read as a date. (The PWA's own tab bar was already right: it uses a filled car, which is why this survived on the shelf alone.) The chat panel's *The Day's Driving* heading carried the same calendar glyph and moved with it. Guarded by `scenario_no_two_shelf_buttons_wear_the_same_icon`, which diffs every NAV_ITEMS path set — the collision was invisible to read (90 characters of curve data nobody diffs) and trivial to test.
- **Boards can wear shelf-matched stroked icons.** The shelf draws the app's own destinations as stroked 24×24 SVGs and drew boards as whatever emoji the household typed — two optical languages on one row. `BOARD_ICONS` (home_board.py) is a curated set of Heroicon-style path sets; a board stores `icon:<key>` in its icon field (any other value is still emoji text, nobody's 🗂️ changes). Resolution is server-side for the shelf (`page_summaries` ships `icon_paths`), client-side in the editor (`catalog()` ships `board_icons`; `boardIconHtml()` draws chips, tab rows and the picker — emoji text is HTML-escaped since it rides x-html). The icon field became a picker: the stroked set plus an emoji input. *(v2.310.0)* It shipped as **eighteen**, which is a sample rather than a set — a household naming a board "Homework" or "Grandma's" found nothing that fit and fell back to an emoji, which is exactly the ragged row the stroked set exists to prevent. **Sixty-three now**, all Heroicons-v1 outline like NAV_ITEMS so the shelf stays one language, and **grouped** (Places / Time / People / Home / Media / Signals / Work) — sixty glyphs in one undifferentiated wrap is a worse picker than eighteen were, so the labels are what make the bigger set faster to search rather than slower. `BOARD_ICON_GROUPS` is the source of truth and the flat `BOARD_ICONS` is derived from it, so **no stored `icon:<key>` depends on which group its icon sits in** and icons can be regrouped freely; `catalog()` ships `group` on each row and the picker builds its sections from that (capped at `max-h-56`, or a set this size shoves the settings dialog off screen). A test walks every path with a real SVG tokeniser — arcs pack their flags, so a naive number regex misreads them — because a typo in a `d` is a garbage glyph on somebody's wall and nothing else in the app would catch it.
- **The calendar card's scrollbar is gone from the wall.** The v2.207 component mount moved the agenda's scroller out of `.tile-scroll`'s reach and a platform scrollbar appeared inside the tile. `.board-calendar`-scoped rules hide scrollbars on the component's scrollers (`.cal-agenda-grid`, `.fc-scroller`) wherever a board mounts one — same wall rule, touch and wheel still work. The `/calendar` page keeps its own slim themed scrollbars.
- Also fixed: the idle return on `/board/<slug>` navigated relatively to `board/home` (which only rendered by the grace of `find_page`'s fallback); it now climbs through `_up` like every other nav link.

## The chrome became tiles (v2.209.0)

- **The clock strip, the hero band and a page heading are tile types now** — `clock`, `hero`, `heading` in the catalog, drawn in `board_tile_body.html` with every other body. Until now they were hardcoded template markup above the grid, on every board unconditionally: every "new" board was a copy of the home page, and the strip was beyond the reach of every layout tool. Now the grid is the whole page, and the home board is just a board — any board can be rebuilt to look exactly like it, or like nothing else.
- **Migration preserves every wall.** Pages carry a schema version: a stored page without `v` was drawn under the chrome, so `_page_from` prepends `clock` and `hero` full-width (spans `{cols: columns, rows: 1}`) at read time — lazy, into a COPIED spans dict (mutating the stored one would be the read-time rewrite this layer promises never to do). The editor saves `v: 2`, which is what stops the migration running twice. A v2 board means what it says — and a NEW board (`blankPage`) says blank.
- **The chrome types are always-truthy builders** (`_tile_clock` carries the forecast days, `_tile_hero` is a placement marker for the payload's top-level `hero`, `_tile_heading` carries its scale) — a board that asked for a clock must never lose it to a quiet day. They are `BARE_TILES` (no panel: the strip floats, the band draws its own rounded card, a heading is ink), pageless (not doors), and draw **no heading row at all** (`x-if`, not `x-show` — a hidden row still answers querySelector). A heading tile's text IS its title (untitled reads "Heading", visibly asking to be typed into); its size option is Page title / Section.
- **Weather un-suppressed where it is honest**: a board WITH a clock tile hides its weather tile (the strip already carries the forecast); a board withOUT one keeps it — the household took the strip off, not the forecast. Chrome defaults to full board width when added (`defaultCols(type)`); everything else keeps the quarter.
- **Behaviour change, deliberate**: a `?widgets=` URL override is literal now — it never gets chrome it did not name.
- Tests: the legacy-upgrade scenario asserts chrome-as-tiles with the original four tiles and their order intact; a new scenario pins v1-gains-chrome / v2-means-what-it-says / no-double-injection; fixtures that are not about migration declare `v: 2`; the render fixture gained a hero tile and the blank-install property excludes chrome alongside containers.

## Blank means blank, for tiles too (v2.210.0)

- **A built-in tile's wall heading is the typed title and nothing else.** Until now an empty title field fell back to the type's wall sentence ("The rest of the day", "What's coming"), which meant a heading could never be REMOVED — the same trap cards escaped in v2.204.1. `_build_tile` now prints `built['title']` alone; an untitled tile draws no heading row at all (and no icon — the row is the heading).
- **v3 migration keeps every wall's words.** `_page_from` writes the old fallback (`heading` or `label`) into each v<3 tile's empty title field, so nothing on an existing wall changes — the field finally matches the wall, and clearing it finally works. Chrome (`BARE_TILES`) and containers never had the fallback and stay blank. The editor saves `v: 3`.
- A tile from a `?widgets=` URL override goes through no migration, so untitled there means blank — consistent with v2.209's overrides-are-literal rule. The untitled `heading` TILE keeps its "Heading" placeholder in the body (an invisible empty bare tile could not be found to edit); its text still comes only from its title.
- Tests: the wall-label scenario flipped to pin the new rule (untitled → blank, typed title printed, wall sentences still sensible as backfill values); the migration scenarios assert the backfilled title rides beside the household's own config and that chrome grew none.

## The chores kiosk split into cards (v2.211.0)

- **Three cards, one drawing each.** The chores kiosk's three drawings are board cards now: the points **leaderboard** (the existing `chores` tile, untouched), the per-child **`chores_lanes`**, and the pooled-reward **`chores_rewards`** (family goals). The lanes and the goals strip were extracted from chores.html into `components/chores_lanes.html` as Jinja macros — the kiosk page and the board render the SAME macros, so the wall can never drift from the page.
- **The contract is the arrays.** `choresLanesLogic(apiBase)` (one copy, in the component) carries the four arrays (balances/chores/rewards/redemptions), the slicing helpers, and the kiosk actions; `choresPage()` spreads it in and keeps only its own enrichment (`lanesOnBalances` hook: point tools, ledgers, the kiosk status celebration). **Identity stays per-lane** — every action passes the tapped child's `member_id` from its own lane, never stored.
- **Data rule 2 held**: the lanes card SELF-FETCHES via `choresLanesCard` (an interactive card cannot ride a payload that rebuilds under the finger typing a chip-in amount; refresh on the kiosk's own 30s cadence, `members` config filters the lanes); the goals card RIDES the payload (`_tile_chores_goals` ships pooled rewards in the same shape the kiosk fetches live, pool status resolved server-side).
- **Rule 3 started**: `chores_lanes` is the first card to carry the **`interactive`** option. Default OFF — a wall is a display first; OFF draws no buttons at all (x-if, not hidden). The macro takes the gate as a parameter, so the page's kiosk is unconditionally interactive.
- Both new types are PAGELESS (the lanes hold their own buttons — legal inside the tile's `<a>` only while it has no href). Unconfigured household (no chores and no rewards / no pooled rewards) → the cards vanish like any unconfigured feature. home.html now includes the lanes logic + kid_glyphs.
- Tests: test_chores_lanes_render (the extraction's safety net, 3 real-DOM scenarios) passes on the macro-rendered page unchanged; a new home-board scenario pins the mount config, the goals payload shape, the interactive default, and the unconfigured vanish.

## Lanes with buttons, and sections as toggles (v2.212.0)

- **The lanes card is interactive by default now** (user decision): an inert lanes card is the leaderboard with extra steps — the card's whole purpose is the tap. `interactive: off` remains for walls that really are displays.
- **THE CONVERSION PARADIGM, adopted**: every part of a page's drawing becomes a boolean toggle on its card, all on by default so zero-config equals the page. The lane's five parts — Name & points (`show_header`), Family goals, Rewards, Claimed chores, Available chores — are card options; the macro gates each on `laneShow(part)`, the logic's default answers true (the kiosk page), the card answers from `t.data.parts` with absent-means-shown (a card saved before a part existed keeps drawing everything). This is the pattern every future page→card conversion carries: members filter + section toggles + interactive where there are taps.
- Clarified: the Chores page itself is still a regular page — it renders the same shared macros as the cards (v2.211) but is not yet a thin board; its kiosk mode is unconditionally interactive.

## The gutter stopped being a secret (v2.213.0)

- **Row heights have no minimum — but the gutter made it look like one.** `row_height` genuinely clamps 1–10000, yet a board at 1px rows still stepped ~17px per added row: the grid drew a hardcoded Tailwind `gap-4` (16px) between tracks, and a tile spanning R rows crosses R−1 gutters. Nothing in the editor said so.
- **The gutter is the board's third grid number now**: `gap` (0–100, default 16 = the old look) lives on the page beside `columns` and `row_height`, rides the payload, and has its own editor field ("Tiles sit N pixels apart"). 0 is legal and means seamless — so 1px rows with a 0 gap give true pixel-granularity tile heights. Absent means 16, so no stored board changes. The row-height label now says the gaps count inside a multi-row tile's height, and `_cell()` still measures the live grid so arranging tracks whatever the household set.

## Row stepping and spacing, untangled (v2.214.0)

- **Why they were intertwined**: a CSS grid span occupies its tracks PLUS the gutters between them, so with a structural `row-gap` a span-R tile drew `R×row_height + (R−1)×gap` — the step per row was the SUM of the two settings, and fine height control with nice spacing was impossible by construction.
- **The gutter left the vertical skeleton**: `row-gap: 0`, tracks step by exactly `row_height`, and the spacing is painted as a bottom inset on every tile (`#tile-grid > a { margin-bottom: var(--tile-gap) }`). A tile now draws `R×row_height − gap`; **v4 migration adds one gap to every stored row height**, which makes the old and new formulas equal for every span count — no wall changed by a pixel. Columns keep a real `column-gap` (widths are fractions, not steps). `_cell().row` is now exactly `rowHeight()`, so a resize drag steps by what the editor says a row is. Editor labels updated: "a 2-row tile is exactly twice this" / "spacing only, never part of a tile's height".
- **Arrange mode stopped lying about heights**: the heading row is no longer force-shown on untitled tiles while arranging (borrowed height made accurate resizing impossible). A floating nameplate (`.tile-arrange-badge`, absolutely positioned, no pointer, no layout space) carries the tile's name and its "C × R" readout instead.

## A tile is its rows, at any gutter (v2.215.0)

- **v2.214's inset model had a wart the family found in a day**: the tile's box was `R×row_height − gap`, so changing the gutter after sizing tiles resized them — bottoms pinned to the lattice, tops walking down. Not intuitive, and rightly reported as such.
- **The vertical lattice is 1px tracks now.** `spanStyle` converts rows to pixels itself (`grid-row: span R×row_height + gap`, minus the constant painted inset), so a tile's drawn box is **exactly `R × row_height` regardless of the gutter** — change the spacing and the tiles move apart; nothing changes size. The drag still steps by one row (`_cell().row = rowHeight()`), and columns keep their real `column-gap`.
- **v5 migration**: the v4 one-release row-height padding is taken back off (`v==4` boards only: `row_height −= gap`); boards that skipped v4 keep their numbers untouched — a stored row height finally needs no adjustment ever, because the box formula no longer references the gutter. Multi-row tiles on never-resaved pre-v4 boards give up the gutters their spans used to swallow, which is the point of the whole change.

## The column gutters were the same disease (v2.215.1)

- Reported off the wall within the hour: with the row axis fixed, changing the gutter warped WIDTHS — on a fine column grid the structural `column-gap` shrank the fr tracks toward zero and a C-span tile's width became dominated by its C−1 crossed gutters, so tiles got wider as the gutter grew.
- Both gutters are painted now. `column-gap: 0`; a column's pitch is exactly `board ÷ columns`; each tile wears half a gutter per side (adjacent tiles sit one gutter apart, the board edges get a symmetric half-gutter inset, nothing bleeds off the page) plus the full gutter below. **A tile gives up exactly one gutter of width and of height, never one per span.** Width cannot be fully gutter-independent the way height now is — the board cannot grow sideways — but growing the gutter shrinks every tile by the same constant and moves them apart, which is what a gutter means. `_cell()` simplifies to `width/cols` and `rowHeight()`: a drag steps by exactly what the editor says. No migration needed — nothing stored references the formulas.

## The divisibility rule, said out loud (v2.215.2)

- Confirmed off the wall: with gutter-independent tile heights (v2.215), a STACK of tiles beside one tall tile bottom-aligns only when the gutter is a multiple of the row height — a tile's lattice footprint is `R×row_height + gap`, so a stack of N carries N gutters where a single neighbour carries one, and the difference `(N−1)×gap` must be worth a whole number of rows. Gap 16 over rows of 10 can never align; rows of 8 under a 16 gutter always do.
- This is the honest price of heights that ignore the gutter: the closed geometries (structural gaps; the v2.214 inset) always aligned but entangled size with spacing, which the family rejected first. The sweet spot is small rows that divide the gutter — fine sizing AND alignment.
- The editor now says so: a warning appears under the gutter field only when the two numbers do not divide, naming the gutters that would line up.

## Every kiosk page is a board (v2.216.0) — kiosk-boards arc, slice 1

- **The panel shelf's buttons opened the ADMIN page.** Tapping Errands on a wall panel gave the page whose top half is a household-task editor, an owner dropdown, a recurrence select and a natural-language errand parser — on a screen with no keyboard, mounted where every child in the house can reach it. Routines was a form per member. The page a browser wants and the page a wall wants are not the same page, and only one of them was ever served.
- **Each destination now has a BOARD**, shipped in `home_board.BUILTIN_PAGES` (`schedule`, `calendar`, `errands`, `shopping`, `occasions`, `chores`, `routines`, `trips`, `map`, `moments`). `intake` is the deliberate exception — mail approval and IMAP settings stay off shared screens. `home` is not in the list: it is the household's own board already.
- **`?panel=true` on a destination draws its board**, from the same `home.html` the `/home` and `/board/{slug}` routes use (`main._page_or_board`). The address does not change, so a tablet bookmarked on `/errands?panel=true` gets the better screen with nothing re-pointed. Three ways out, all already spelled: no `?panel=true` (a browser gets the page it always got), `?kiosk=true` (the pages that grew their own kiosk mode before boards existed answer to it, untouched — retiring a family's daily surface before anybody has stood in front of the new one is a surprise, not a migration), and `/board/<slug>` (the same board with the editor under it, which is where "Open to edit ↗" points).
- **Authored, not defaults (v2.229.0 — this replaces the fork model).** The ten live in `services/builtin_boards.json`, loaded at import by `home_board._load_builtin_pages()`, and they always win. `normalize_pages` DROPS any stored page whose slug is a shipped board's — on read, never by rewriting settings — so the forks every install accumulated are inert rather than deleted. The editor no longer merges them into its draft, so they cannot be edited or saved; `_shippedPristine` and `cleanPages`'s JSON-string comparison are gone with the model they guarded. `/api/home_board/pages` still answers `{pages, shipped}`, but `shipped` is now ALL ten (it used to be only the untouched ones, so a household that forked a board stopped being shown ours — the fork hid what it forked from). **Why the inversion:** "stored wins" sounded generous and behaved as a trap — editing a board forked it silently and it stopped tracking every improvement shipped afterwards; by the time it was noticed, all ten had forked on the dev install and none tracked anything. A household changes a shipped board by DUPLICATING it into a board of their own. **The picture stayed the household's (v2.229.1).** B0 took the per-board background away with editability and that was wrong — a picture is presentation, not content, and the tiles being ours never made the photograph ours. `panel_shipped_backgrounds` (`{slug: picture}`, shipped boards only) restores it, applied in `builtin_page()` and carried by `backgrounds()`. Precedence: household pick → authored picture → `panel_background`; blank means "no answer" and falls back rather than blanking. **Why this is not the `panel_page_backgrounds` map deleted in v2.227.0:** that one was a second HOUSEHOLD setting racing the board's own editable field, and it won, so the visible field did nothing. The rule here is one field per board decided by ownership — an own board keeps its `background` field and never appears in the map; a shipped board has no household-editable field, so the map IS it. Editor: a row per shipped board in `#panel-setup` (`shippedBoards()`/`setShippedBackground()`), where clearing a row deletes the key rather than storing an empty string. **The file lives beside `home_board.py`, not in `chauffeur/data/`** — that directory is git-ignored as a secrets folder, so a boards file there never reaches the repo and the add-on builds with none (the loader degrades to `{}` silently by design); `scenario_the_shipped_boards_actually_ship` guards existence, count and ignore-status.
- **`columns` is stated (12) on every built-in board** rather than inherited: a span is a count of columns, so a household on a 24-column home board would otherwise get all ten of these at half width. Row height and gutter still follow the household.
- **A destination's board is never a second shelf button.** `home_board.own_boards()` — every page that is neither `home` nor a `BUILTIN_PAGES` slug — is what the shelf, `resolve_tabs`, `_with_boards` and the catalog's tab picker all read. Without it, editing the Errands board grew a second Errands button beside the first one.
- `home.html` learns which board it is from `<body data-board-slug>`, NOT from a Jinja expression inside its script: the jsdom harnesses execute that script as plain JavaScript, and `{{ … }}` in it is a syntax error that takes every board runtime test down at once.
- Tests: `tests/test_builtin_boards.py`.

## The errands lists became cards (v2.217.0) — kiosk-boards arc, slice 2

- **The complaint that started the arc**: the errands panel view was the admin view. What a wall needs is the two lists and a tick to mark something done; what it got was a household-task editor, an owner dropdown, a recurrence select, a natural-language errand parser and two modals.
- **`components/errand_lists.html`** now owns both drawings — `task_list(interactive, edit, remove)` and `errand_list(interactive, edit)` macros over one `errandListsLogic(apiBase)`. The errands PAGE renders them (it is Alpine now, for those two lists only) and so do the new `task_list` / `errand_list` board cards, so the wall can never drift from the page. Everything the macros do not draw — the add rows, both editor modals, the location autocomplete, the driver/passenger constraint toggles — stays page-only plain script.
- **The editors are ABSENT from a card, not hidden.** `edit`/`remove` are hook expressions: the page passes `openTaskEditor` / `deleteTask` / `openEditModal`, a card passes nothing, and the button is never drawn. A wall panel is reachable by every child in the house and `x-show` is not a permission model. `openTaskEditor(t)` and `deleteTask(t)` take the TASK now, not its id — looking it back up was the only reason the page kept a second copy of the list.
- **Both cards SELF-FETCH** (board rule 2, same as `chores_lanes`): the board payload is cached 20s, and a tick-box that comes back unticked because the wall is still serving a pre-tap answer is worse than no tick-box. The builders (`_tile_task_list`, `_tile_errand_list`) ship CONFIG only, plus the one question a client cannot answer — a household that has never made a task gets no tile at all. Poll cadence 30s, the kiosk's.
- **The conversion paradigm applied**: `interactive` on by default; section toggles `show_load`/`show_due`/`show_owner`/`show_recurrence` and `show_past_due`/`show_open`/`show_completed`/`show_location`/`show_when`, all defaulting on so zero-config equals the page; owner filter and `unclaimed_only` on the task card. The row cap is applied PER BAND so a long completed list can never push the past-due band off a wall. `past_due_only` still wins over the section toggles.
- The shipped `errands` board is these two side by side (the "do something / go somewhere" distinction is only learnable with both in view), with `show_completed: False` — the one place the paradigm's default is overridden, and overridden in the BOARD rather than in the option so the toggle keeps meaning "the page shows this".
- **A trap worth knowing for every future conversion**: Alpine INVOKES an expression whose result is a function (it is how `x-text="someMethod"` works), so `x-if="openEditModal"` opened the editor once per row while the page drew itself. Hook expressions are tested as `!!(expr)`.
- The old `errands` and `tasks` tiles are untouched — they are the four-row GLANCE a home board wants, and these are the page's actual lists.
- Tests: `tests/test_errand_lists_render.py` (jsdom).

## The shopping kiosk became three cards (v2.218.0) — kiosk-boards arc, slice 3

- The Meals shelf button opened a PLANNER: dish repertoire, rules drawer, photo picker, Walmart cart, every meals setting. The page's own `?kiosk=true` mode had known the right answer for a year — it hid everything except the week's dinners, the "we've run out of this" chips and the list. Those three are now cards.
- **`components/shopping_lists.html`** owns the drawings — `week_board(source)`, `staple_chips(interactive)`, `shopping_items(interactive, remove, clear)` over two factories, `mealWeekLogic(apiBase)` (the composed week + every day helper: `mainDish`, `dayHeadline`, `daySides`, `dayImage`, `dayTint`, `dayEffort`, `daySqueeze`) and `shoppingListsLogic(apiBase)` (lists/items/runs/staples + `setChecked`, `outOf`, `isOnList`, `byline`). `shoppingPage()` spreads both and its copies are gone; the `meals_week` / `shopping_staples` / `shopping_list` cards wrap them.
- **NOTHING shared is a getter, and that is load-bearing.** `{...factory()}` EVALUATES a getter on the way past, so a shared `get open()` would arrive at the page as a frozen array and nothing would error. Everything shared is a METHOD (`openItems()`, `checkedItems()`, `weekDays()`, `boardDays()`); the page keeps thin `get open()` / `get checked()` / `get allDays()` in its own literal, where nothing spreads them, so its markup is untouched.
- **The wall can never re-plan dinner.** The shared `loadMealWeek` is a GET of `api/meals/week`; `compose_week` reads the cache and the plates and persists nothing (asserted in the test by inspecting the source). `repropose` is a POST and stays on the page, behind a button somebody presses. The page's `loadWeek(repropose)` now POSTs then delegates to the shared read.
- Destructive controls are hook expressions again: the page passes `remove`/`clear` (and still gates them on `!isKiosk`), a card passes nothing so the ✕ and Clear are absent from the DOM. Section toggles: `show_image`/`show_sides`/`show_effort`/`show_squeeze` on the week; `show_runs`/`show_cart`/`show_note`/`show_byline` on the list; `show_hint` on the chips. Both list cards take a `list` option to pin one list. All three self-fetch (60s for the list, 15 min for the week — a wall that nobody touches must roll over on its own).
- Tapping a staple chip stays exactly what it was: a line on the list for THIS shop, tap again to undo, and never a reclassification of the ingredient — which is why it is safe on a panel the children can reach.
- Fixed on the way past: `control_center.html`'s `fetch('api/telemetry')` had no `apiBase`, so it resolved a directory short on `/board/{slug}`.
- Tests: `tests/test_shopping_cards.py`. Several existing suites now read the page RENDERED or include-inlined (`test_shopping`, `test_meals`, `test_panel_chrome`) — a macro's definition sits outside every x-data root in the file it is written in, so only the rendered page puts its markup where it goes.

## The routines kiosk lanes became a card (v2.219.0) — kiosk-boards arc, slice 4

- The Routines shelf button opened an editing surface: a routine editor per member, a copy-from-somebody-else control, the prep kits. Its own `?kiosk=true` mode already knew the answer — today's checklist per child, ticked off with that child's identity.
- **`components/routine_lanes.html`** owns the lane grid (`lane_grid(interactive)` over a shared `routine_row()` inside) and `routineLanesLogic(apiBase)`: `streaks`, `dayItems`, `formatClock`/`loadClockFormat`, `loadStreaks`, `loadAllDayItems`, `reloadLanes`, `toggleRoutineCheck`. The routines page spreads it in; the `routines_lanes` card wraps it.
- **Identity is per lane**, unchanged and re-asserted: every check takes the tapped child's `s.member_id` from its own lane, passed per call, never stored — two children at one kiosk are two lanes in use at once. The server re-validates that the routine belongs to them.
- **The celebration stays on the PAGE.** `maybeCelebrateStatusKiosk` is a full-screen overlay; four lane cards on a wall each firing one is a fault, not a party. The shared logic exposes `lanesOnStreaks` / `lanesOnChecked` hooks that default to no-ops and the page overrides both — which also keeps the shared script from reaching for a helper (`components/status_celebration.html`) a board need not include.
- **A row is a `<button>` where it can be tapped and a `<div>` where it cannot.** Alpine has no dynamic tag, so the two are separate `x-if` branches over one `routine_row()` macro. An inert card drawing dead buttons reads as broken rather than as a display.
- Section toggles `show_header`/`show_status`/`show_streak`/`show_progress`/`show_items`, members filter, `interactive` on by default. `laneColumns()` caps at 4 on a card (the page measures its window).
- The shipped `routines` board is `kids` (the day preview each child gets) then `routines_lanes` — the kiosk's own order. The streak leaderboard is not on it because each lane carries its own 🔥, which is what the kiosk decided.
- Tests: `tests/test_routine_lanes.py` (jsdom). Repaired two long-stale assertions on the way past: `test_nav` still expected the pre-v2.193 `SHELF_ITEMS` loop, and `test_board_ha_tiles` matched the PAGELESS list as a literal line (it is checked as a set now — it grows with every conversion).

## A tile can be as tall as its content (v2.220.0) — kiosk-boards arc, slice 5

Four things went wrong on the wall at once, reported together.

- **`rows` is a promise about height that a list cannot keep.** Four children with eleven routine items each is a different height every morning, so a typed number is either short (the wall cuts the last child off — how all four boards shipped) or tall (a band of empty panel). A tile's span now takes **`auto`**: `spanStyle` spends MEASURED pixels on the same 1px lattice, plus the same one gutter, so a fit tile sits in a row of fixed ones without disturbing them. The editor offers it as a **fit** checkbox beside `rows` (hidden for tiles whose content is laid out INTO them — a map, a timeline, a mosaic, where the height decides the content); dragging a fit tile's bottom edge takes it off fit rather than fighting the measurement.
  - **Measured from the CHILDREN, never the tile's own box.** A tile stretches to the area it was given, so `scrollHeight` reports whatever we last set: it converges upward and can never shrink again. `<template>` children are skipped — Alpine leaves them as zero-height markers and one at the top puts the origin at y=0.
  - **Two observers per tile**, because content arrives two ways: these cards SELF-FETCH (MutationObserver) and the board is responsive (ResizeObserver). Either alone is right on the first paint and wrong after. Observers live outside Alpine like `boardMaps`, are re-bound when Alpine replaces an element, and are dropped when a tile leaves the board.
  - Every shipped board's list tiles are `auto` now; `drives`, `calendar`, `map`, `trips`, `moments` keep stated rows.
- **A board never loses the card it is about.** Rule 1 hides a feature nobody has set up — right on a mixed board, wrong on a board ABOUT that feature. An Errands board with no errands card is a half-empty screen that reads as broken, which is how it reached a wall. Builtin widgets carry `require: True`; `_build_tile` substitutes `REQUIRED_EMPTY[type]` instead of returning None. **The editor was undoing this (fixed v2.228.2).** `toInstances` — the editor's mirror of `normalize_instances`, under a comment claiming the two could not drift — rebuilt every instance as `{id, type, config}` and dropped `require`. `loadSetup` runs each page through it, so merely OPENING the editor stripped the flag off all ten shipped boards and a quiet Chores board went blank instead of saying it was quiet. Two normalisers for one shape is the actual defect; `test_board_instances.py` now pins the flag through both the load and the save path.
- **The kids strip was being folded into a hero that was not there.** `build()` lifted the `kids` tile into `hero.kids` unconditionally; the Routines board has no hero band, so the digest went into an object nothing on that page draws and vanished with no error. The fold is now conditional on the board actually having a hero tile.
- **The editor lists the shipped boards.** A board you cannot find is a board you cannot fix, and fixing the heights was the first thing anybody wanted. `/api/home_board/pages` answers `{pages, shipped}` — stored and the rest, kept separate so the editor does not write all ten into settings on the first save. `cleanPages()` drops any shipped board that still matches the pristine copy the server sent (one string comparison, not a dirty flag a dozen edit paths would have to remember). The single-page endpoint added in v2.216 is gone with its only caller.
- **The load sentence says what it counts.** It was "16 of the 32 things done in the last 30 days were Celma's" over a task list where nothing had ever been ticked — the total is `tasks + drives`, and the wording named neither. It reads "drives and jobs" now.

## Fit was measuring the wrong elements (v2.220.1)

- Reported off the wall twice in a row: every fit tile collapsed to its heading, then read as "fit does nothing — still the Rows height". Both are the same bug. The measurement walked the tile's DIRECT children and took the first one's `top` and the last one's `bottom`, and a tile's direct children are not its content:
  - `<template>` — Alpine's marker, no box, real node inserted beside it;
  - **`<div class="contents">` — the built-in tile's body wrapper.** It is `display: contents` on purpose (a box between a mosaic and its tile is a box that ends up zero pixels tall), so it has NO BOX and a browser hands back zeros for it. That is the child holding all the content;
  - the arrange nameplate and the resize grip — `x-show`, so present and `display: none` except while arranging, absolutely positioned when shown. The LAST child, and the one whose zero `bottom` the measurement was reading.
- `autoFlowBoxes` now descends through `display: contents`, skips `display: none` and out-of-flow (`absolute`/`fixed`) children, and `autoTileHeight` takes the UNION of what is left rather than first-to-last — after all that, the content is not reliably the last child either.
- **The jsdom board probes could not have caught this**, and that is worth knowing before trusting one again: jsdom does no layout, so every rect is already a fiction and a measurement reading the WRONG elements looks exactly like one reading the right ones. `tests/test_fit_to_content.py` drives the real function against a hand-built tile with the boxes stated — reverting the fix turns it red.
- Also pinned there: `auto` survives the round trip (editor span → `panel_pages` → `_page_from` → `normalize_instances` → board payload). `panel_pages` is `List[Any]`, so nothing along the way coerces a span back to two integers, but nothing said so either.

## The kid digest is one drawing (v2.221.0)

- Reported off the wall: the Routines board's kid digest was a flat name-and-lines list, not the lane cards the page's kiosk strip draws. Root cause is instructive: the `kids` TILE predates the digest strip, and nobody ever saw its drawing because **every board with a hero folds the kids into the hero band** (`build()` lifts the tile into `hero.kids`). The Routines board was the first board without a hero to show the tile, and it surfaced the stale drawing — months of drift, invisible until v2.220 stopped stripping it.
- **`components/kid_digest_lanes.html`** now owns the strip: `digest_grid()` macro (day-label heading, weather line, a lane card per child — avatar, name, streak 🔥, ride lines, "No rides — free day! 🎉", task lines, routine count) over the contract `digestCards()/digestColumns()/digestLabel()/digestWeather()`. The routines page answers it from its self-fetched `kidDigests`; the `kids` tile answers it via `kidDigestCard(t)` from the tile payload it rides (display only — board rule 2's payload side, unlike the interactive lanes beside it).
- **The hero band's kid columns are deliberately NOT this drawing**: inside the hero they are a compact strip under the next drive — no avatars, no streaks — sized for a band. Same data, two intentional renderings, one incidental one now deleted.
- `_tile_kids` fixes found on the way: digest entries carry no `member_id`, so the tile's **members filter compared against a missing field and silently emptied every filtered tile** — the id is folded in from the dict key now; kids with a quiet day but real tasks/routines were dropped (`lines`-only test) though the page shows them; `weather` now rides the payload; lanes sort by name, the page's order. The shipped Routines board's kids tile drops its typed title ("Each kid") — the drawing's own "☀️ Today / 🌙 Tomorrow" heading is better information — and sets `lines: 8`, since the page does not truncate a kid's day.
- Pinned in `tests/test_routine_lanes.py`: both surfaces render the macro, neither keeps a private copy, and the builder speaks the contract. Note for future assertions: `tpl_source` inlines `include`, not `import` — a macro expands only where it is CALLED, so markup checks against an importing page must use the RENDERED page.

## The calendar card is interactive (v2.222.0)

- Due since `?panel=true` on /calendar started serving the board: the card IS the calendar page's content now, and the page's one irreplaceable tap is opening an event. The board's `syncCalendars` had the page's two affordances hardcoded off ("they become card options the day a card wants them" — that day).
- `interactive` (default ON, the paradigm) mounts the shared component with `details: true` — tapping an event opens the component's own details dialog, in place, never a navigation. `show_legend` (default ON) mounts `legend: true` — the per-person chips, whose taps hide a person on that card only. Both are mount options the component already had; the card just never passed them. List view (payload-built, no taps) is unaffected.
- **An interactive calendar tile is NOT a door.** `opens()` takes the TILE now, not its type: an `<a>` around events that open a dialog would navigate mid-overlay. Decided per instance — display-only calendar cards stay doors.
- `syncCalendars` also keys mounted instances by their mount CONFIG (`_liveCalendars` is a Map id→key), fixing a latent bug: changing a card's view (or toggling interactive) in the editor was ignored until a full page reload, because "already mounted" was decided by id alone.
- Verified in a real DOM with the vendored FullCalendar: event renders, tile has no `href`, tapping the event opens the details overlay with its location, legend chips draw. Pinned in `tests/test_builtin_boards.py`.

## Bare cards, a fit that keeps measuring, and a calendar you can read (v2.223.0)

- **The kid digest card no longer draws the weather.** There is a weather CARD; a drawing that quietly includes another card's content is how a board says the same thing twice with no way to turn one off. The digest keeps its day label; `_tile_kids` stops shipping `weather`.
- **Every card can drop its own panel** — the card-level twin of the custom tile's `bare`. `_build_card` resolves `bare` for any type and the cell wears the SAME `data-plain` no-surface state a nested stack's cell already wore (one plain state, not two). Offered in the card's ⚙ rather than declared per type in the catalog: it is a property of being a card in a tile, not of any one drawing. The card gear is unconditional now — every card has at least this to ask. **This is what makes the composition the user asked for possible**: a custom tile holding a bare weather card and a bare kid-digest card is the old combined drawing, with no duplicated functionality and each half independently removable.
- **Fit stopped measuring after the first paint inside custom tiles.** The ResizeObserver watched only the tile — whose height WE impose — so content growing inside it (a hosted HA card settling, an image arriving in a cell, a font swap rewrapping) resized nothing observed and mutated nothing either. It now observes the tile (width rewraps) AND every flow box, re-collected on each mutation since Alpine replaces them wholesale. No feedback loop: our span write resizes only the tile, and the boxes are content-sized.
- **A vendored grid has to be restated for every theme.** FullCalendar's chrome is styled in hardcoded near-white — right for the dark page it was written on — and the component carried a `body.ha-theme` remap and NOTHING for the panel skin. Panel mode deliberately runs no HA theming, so on a light wall the month title, weekday headers, day numbers, toolbar buttons and "+N more" chips were white-on-paper. Reported as "can you tell what month the calendar is showing? Me neither." Now a `html[data-panel]` block in the skin's own tokens, so one block serves both panel themes; the active view button keeps the accent so which view you are in reads across a kitchen. Pinned in `test_panel_chrome.py`, including that the block uses tokens rather than hardcoded colours.

## Fit on custom tiles, and the digest's hardcoded heading (v2.223.1)

- **Fit did nothing on custom tiles** — the tile drew at whatever `rows` said. `syncAutoTiles` walked `drawnTiles()`, which flattens the board to CARDS. A built-in tile's card keeps the TILE's id (the card IS the tile), so the element lookup found it and fit worked; a custom tile's cards are namespaced `tileid-cardid`, so the tile's own id was never in that list, never looked up, never observed. **A span is a property of a TILE**, so it walks `tiles()` now. Reverting the fix turns the new scenario red with the reported symptom.
  - This is the second bug from the same helper name. `drawnTiles()` returning cards is right for `syncMap`/`syncCalendars`/`syncTimeline` (they mount per CARD) and wrong for anything reasoning about spans, size or position.
  - Pinned by a second harness in `tests/test_fit_to_content.py`: a whole board in jsdom with stub observers recording which TILE elements got watched. jsdom does no layout so it can say nothing about heights — but "was this tile measured at all" is structural, and that is what both custom-tile reports turned out to be.
- **The kid digest's "☀️ Today" was hardcoded chrome.** It was an `<h3>` inside the card — a second label in a box whose heading belongs to its TILE (blank means blank, v2.204.1/v2.210), and nothing in the editor could remove it. It is a small dim caption now, not a heading, and the card finally got the conversion paradigm it predates: `show_day`, `show_header`, `show_streak`, `show_tasks`, `show_routines`, all defaulting on so zero-config still equals the page. The day caption stays available because the strip flips between today and tomorrow at the evening cutover, and a digest of tomorrow's rides read as today's is worse than a caption — but it is one toggle away now.

## A fit tile cannot stay wrong (v2.223.2)

Third report on the same feature, so this stops enumerating signals and adds a floor.

- **The observers were missing style-only changes.** The MutationObserver watched `childList`/`characterData` but not `attributes`, and half of what changes a tile's height here is a STYLE: the kid digest sets its column count with `:style="grid-template-columns: repeat(N…)"`, so a strip that arrives as one column (very tall) and settles into four (short) rewraps without adding or removing a single node. No record, no re-measure, tile keeps the tall number. `attributes: true` now.
- **A backstop on the clock that is already ticking.** Every cut of this has failed identically — measured by events, one event does not fire, the measurement lands once and the tile is wrong for the life of the page. A wall panel is up for weeks, so "wrong until something happens to it" is broken. `remeasureAutoTiles()` sweeps every watched tile once a second from `tick()`; the observers stay because they are what makes it feel instant. Cost is one layout read per fit tile per second.
- **The arrange nameplate says what it measured** — `12 × fit · 487px`, or `measuring…` when nothing has landed. Twice a fit tile came out wrong with nothing on screen to distinguish "measured the wrong thing" from "never measured", which are different bugs to go looking for.
- Confirmed on the way: `.contents{display:contents}` really is in the compiled sheet (the built-in tiles' flex chain depends on it), and the walk collects the right element set on a real custom tile.

## The tile was fitting; the card could not (v2.223.3)

- "Says 512px but it's way too tall for the content" — and the tile was RIGHT. A card in a custom tile is given `height: rows * --nc-row` whenever it has `rows`, the only thing that ever SET rows was dragging the card's grip in arrange mode, and **nothing anywhere could put it back**. A card left at a dragged height makes its tile faithfully fit that height, which reads exactly like the tile's fit being broken.
- `rows: 0` has always meant "as tall as the content" — it simply had no control. The card row in the editor now carries a **rows** input (shown only when the card has one) and a **fit** checkbox that returns it to 0, matching the tile's own control.
- The tile's arrange nameplate says why it is tall: `12 × fit · 512px · 1 card sized`. The fix is one level down and nothing else pointed at it.
- Three reports, three different causes, one feature: the measurement read the wrong elements (v2.220.1), `syncAutoTiles` walked cards instead of tiles (v2.223.1), and the height was coming from a card nobody could resize back (this). The lesson recorded: when a fit tile looks wrong, ask whether the TILE is wrong or whether it is correctly fitting something that is.

## Fit per instance, icons per tile, and three more cards you can tap (v2.224.0)

Three reports in one turn, all about the same gap between what a card IS and what the board lets you say about it.

- **Fit is decided per INSTANCE, not per type.** `fillsTile()` knew only the type, and two types draw two different shapes: a Drives card is a timeline OR a compact list, a calendar card is a mounted grid OR a one-line-per-event list. Both list halves were refused a `fit` they could honour exactly — and a list whose length nobody can type ("however many drives today happens to have") is the case fit was built for. `FLOWS_WHEN` is a predicate per type over the instance's config, and every caller (`isAuto`, `spanStyle`, `spanLabel`, the flex/scroll class, the editor's toggle) now carries `config`. Named by **inclusion** — the one view that flows — rather than by excluding the mounted ones: `agenda` reads like a list and has been a component mount since v2.207, so an exclusion test would have handed it a fit and collapsed it.
- **A drawn CARD with no height of its own gets a floor.** The other half of the same report ("maybe fit could just mean fill the parent"). Inside a custom tile, a map/mounted-calendar/camera card at `rows: 0` collapsed to its own padding: its content is laid out INTO the box, and there was no box. Two fixes, both `fillsTile` one level down — the cell takes `min-height: 4 * --nc-row`, and the card body wrapper takes `flex flex-col` instead of the scroll class. The second was a silent bug of exactly the kind v2.185.0 fixed for tiles: `flex-1` in a non-flex parent does nothing, so a camera card drew a heading over nothing.
- **Every tile can wear its own icon.** `ICON_OPTION`, appended in `catalog()` beside `TITLE_OPTION` for the same reason — it means one thing everywhere. The generic types are what forced it: Custom, Card, Entities, Camera and Web page are 🧩 🃏 🏠 📷 🌐 whatever they are pointed at, so a board with two cameras and a radar was three tiles wearing the same 📷. Capped at 8 characters (a glyph slot, not a second title — but a joined emoji is up to 7 code points and slicing one renders as rubble).
