- **A global FastAPI dependency, not middleware**, because dependencies run after routing: `scope['route'].path` is the TEMPLATE (`/api/members/{member_id}/auth`), so a member id can never be mistaken for part of an authorization decision.
- **`tests/test_auth.py` fails on any unclassified route** — the `settings_registry.audit()` discipline pointed at routes, so the next route added cannot be public by accident, which is exactly how this state was reached. It caught six on its first run, including **`/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json`: an interactive map of all 417 routes with a try-it-out console, served publicly next to an unauthenticated app.** Now parents-only; S8 should consider switching them off outright.
- **The tunnel check fails toward asking for credentials**: cloudflared sets `CF-Connecting-IP` on everything it forwards and an outside caller cannot strip it, so absence of any forwarding header means the request arrived directly (the LAN). That is what keeps Argyle working — a dated local-origin grace, ended by the service token in S7, not a permanently trusted LAN.
- `auth_enforce` is deliberately NOT in `Settings` or the settings registry yet: a registry entry obliges a hand path on a real surface, and the surface that owns this switch is the one S8 builds.

## The token is the identity (v2.248.0 — auth arc S2)

The hole S1's brief named and this closes: **identity was client-asserted.** `POST /api/channels/{id}/messages` took `sender_member_id` from the request body and believed it, so any caller could post as any member — a child as a parent, an outsider as anyone. The per-device token that would have settled it has existed since the roles-and-PINs release and was read by five routes.

- **`auth.acting_member(headers, query, claimed_id)`** resolves who is really calling, with stated precedence: a valid token always wins; a token naming a DIFFERENT member is impersonation, recorded and (once enforcing) refused, because no legitimate surface signs in as one member and acts as another; no token at all falls back to the claim and COUNTS it. That last branch is the entire installed base on the day this shipped, and refusing there would have logged the family out of their own house to fix a bug they did not have.
- **`main._acting_id(request, claimed)`** wraps it at the call sites — send, delete, edit and react on messages — so that when the claim fallback dies in S8 it dies in one place.
- **The PWA now attaches `X-Member-Token` to every same-origin request** (a `window.fetch` wrapper in `app.html`), where before it carried the token on chore verification, rejection and little else. Wrapping fetch rather than editing ~200 call sites is deliberate: a migration that depends on finding every call site silently misses some, and the ones it misses are exactly the ones still trusting the client. Absolute URLs to other hosts are skipped — a family credential must never leave this origin.
- **`GET /api/admin/auth_audit` now reports identity too**: `claimed` counts are the migration's progress bar and should fall toward zero as surfaces send their token; `mismatch` counts are different in kind, since every one is a caller acting as somebody they are not. S8 must not flip while `claimed` is high.
- Tests: `tests/test_auth.py` scenarios g–i (token beats body, the no-token fallback still works and is counted, impersonation refused only when enforcing).

## Accounts — adding a person is creating a user (v2.249.0 — auth arc S3)

The household's call, overruling the picker-and-PIN model: if we are shipping a native app to helpers and grandparents, "pick your face and type four digits" is a kitchen-tablet gesture that does not survive a public origin. **The account IS the `FamilyMember`** — `email`, `password_hash`/`password_salt`, `email_verified` on the existing record, never a parallel `User` table that would drift within a release.

- **Invite → link → password, in one step.** `POST /api/members/{id}/invite` (parent-only from the internet) mints a single-use link and mails it; **the link is returned every time, not only on failure**, because a parent standing next to a grandparent should be able to read it out rather than wait on a mail server. `/account/set-password` is a standalone page with no shell, no nav and no identity — whoever opens it has no session and is in a mail client on a phone. Following a link only we could have mailed to that address IS the proof the address belongs to them, so there is no separate "confirm your email" click proving nothing extra.
- **Links: single-use, invite 7 days, reset 2 hours, and setting a password invalidates every other outstanding link** — an old invite in a forwarded email must not outlive the password it was meant to create. Stored in their own `auth_links` table rather than columns on the member, because an invite and a reset can be outstanding at once and columns would silently overwrite one with the other.
- **PBKDF2-SHA256, 260k iterations, per-record salt** — the same hashing story as the PIN, no new dependency in the add-on image, more iterations because a password faces the internet while a PIN (after S5) only re-opens a trusted device. `_public_member` now strips `password_hash`/`password_salt` and exposes `has_password`: it is the one chokepoint a dozen endpoints go through, and a hash that leaks once is offline-crackable forever.
- **Nothing leaks whether an address exists**: login fails identically for unknown-address and wrong-password, and `/api/account/forgot` always answers `ok`.
- **`services/mailer.py`, with its OWN sender settings** (`smtp_host/port/user/password/from`) and `smtp_use_intake` as a mirror toggle that READS intake's credentials rather than copying them (a copy fossilises a password changed in one place and not the other). Separate by default for a concrete reason: **the intake mailbox analyses every message that arrives**, so invites sent from it would feed their own bounces and out-of-office replies back into the proposal queue. The settings live on Config → People beside the invite button, because a family configures a sender in order to invite somebody. `smtp_from` mismatches are warned about in the form, since providers reject them as a silent bounce.
- **Mail is never a hard dependency** — unconfigured, `send()` reports why and the invite shows a copyable link instead.
- **The bootstrap, stated rather than stumbled into:** this endpoint mints a link that sets somebody's password, so it can never be open — yet it also creates the FIRST account, when no parent has a password and the admin page holds no token. Resolved on the boundary the tunnel check already draws: **allowed from the LAN, parent-only from the internet**, the same dated grace Argyle has, ending when S4 gives the admin page a real login.
- Tests: `tests/test_accounts.py` (9 scenarios). Two test-suite exclusions were added for `set_password.html`, both because it is not a panel destination: it carries no page title frame and no panel skin, on purpose.

## The admin surface gets an identity (v2.250.0 — auth arc S4)

The dashboard and config page had never had one. Defensible while they sat behind HA ingress; not defensible once the app was published to the internet — and it is why `/pin/clear` could not be closed earlier, since there was no token for the page to present.

- **`components/admin_gate.html`**, included by both admin pages so they cannot drift: a fetch wrapper that attaches the member token to every same-origin call, plus three states — signed in (invisible), sign-in (email + password), and **first run**.
- **First run stands on HA INGRESS, not the LAN** (correcting S3's bootstrap). Supervisor does not serve ingress to an anonymous browser, so arriving that way means HA already authenticated the person; opening Chauffeur from the sidebar is proof enough to claim the first parent account, with no mail round trip to yourself. A LAN check was weaker for no benefit — a LAN is every guest phone on the wifi — and it forced the owner to be at home.
- **The safety rule, and it is the whole reason this is not a one-line header check**: `X-Hass-Is-Admin` and friends are trivially forged by anyone who can reach the app, so `auth.arrived_via_ingress()` refuses to believe them on any request that came through cloudflared. Supervisor sits on the other side of that boundary and nothing outside can put itself there. Pinned by `test_accounts.scenario_j`.
- **The grace closes by itself**: `_any_parent_has_password()` gates `/api/account/claim`, so once one parent holds a password the bootstrap shuts permanently. No dated switch to remember.
- **`/api/members/{id}/pin/clear` is parent-gated at last** — clear-then-authenticate was a two-call path to anybody's account, because `member_auth` mints freely once `pin_hash` is gone.
- **Rate limiting moved into storage and grew teeth.** It was a module-level dict, and this project rebuilds the add-on on every release, so patience beat the lockout; it now persists, counts **per IP as well as per member** (an attacker walking the family had a fresh budget for each person), and **doubles its backoff** to an hour rather than resetting to a flat 30 seconds. The IP is read from `CF-Connecting-IP` only — `X-Forwarded-For` is client-supplied, and a rate limit keyed on something the attacker can rotate is decoration.
- Tests: `test_accounts.py` scenarios j–n.

## A morning hour of zero meant six o'clock (v2.250.2)

`run_day_of_traffic_sweep` read `int(settings.get('traffic_morning_hour') or 6)`, and `0 or 6` is `6` — so a household that set the day-of traffic buy to **midnight silently got 6am**. Absent now means 6 and an explicit 0 means midnight, the same absent-vs-zero discipline `panel_idle_return_seconds` already keeps.

Found by a test failing on the clock rather than on a change: `test_day_of_traffic`'s sweep scenario sets the hour to 0 precisely so the morning branch is always due, and it had only ever passed because the suite ran after 6am. Also fixed alongside it: `meals.approve_week` now accepts `today` and threads it into `buy_on_for` — `buy_on_for` and `plan_window` already took the seam and this one call site did not, which made the end-to-end span scenario silently date-dependent.

## The PIN, demoted to what it is good at (v2.251.0 — auth arc S5)

Four digits is a perfectly good "let me back in on the kitchen tablet" and a hopeless "anybody on the internet who knows the family's names". So the PIN is not deleted — it is demoted to **re-opening a device somebody has already vouched for**, the pattern every banking app uses, and the reason kids keep the fast path they actually live in.

- **`trusted_devices`**: a device earns trust when somebody signs in on it with a password (login, invite-accept and first-run claim all vouch), or when a parent names it. Trusting is silent — a prompt asking whether to trust the device you are holding is a question nobody can answer better than the act of signing in already did.
- **`POST /api/members/{id}/auth` now needs trusted ground**: a known `X-Device-Id`, or ingress/LAN (where the wall panel and the kitchen tablet live). Off it, the refusal **names the way in** — "sign in with your email and password on this device first, after that your PIN will open it" — because a locked door with no sign on it is how people conclude the app is broken. Dark until S8: today it records `untrusted-pin` in the audit instead of refusing.
- **`X-Device-Id`** is minted once per install and never rotated, sent by both shells. It names the DEVICE, never the person, and carries no credential of its own: the server only asks whether it is on the trusted list.
- **Parent hand path**: Config → People → Trusted devices, showing who vouched for each one and when it was last used ("the one nobody has touched since March" is how a person actually identifies a tablet they no longer own), with Revoke.
- **Stage-driven accounts** (A4's capability table, so no surface has to know a birthday): `own_account` is False for Sprout and Explorer — a five-year-old has no inbox and requiring one to appear on the family's schedule would be absurd — and True for Navigator and Copilot. Offered, never forced: a Navigator with no email keeps the PIN and loses nothing. The Navigator GRANTS line now says an account is what is new, because growing up is granted rather than silently switched.
- Tests: `test_accounts.py` scenarios o–q.

## A panel is a place, not a person (v2.253.0 — auth arc S6)

A wall panel must come up after a power cut at 6am with nobody in the room, so it can never hold a member's session. It holds a **device token** instead: board reads and the interactive board actions a wall legitimately performs (claim a chore, check a routine, play music), and never admin. It gets the powers of the room it is bolted to, not the powers of whoever last walked past it.

**THE DEVICE ASKS; A PARENT ANSWERS.** v2.252.0 shipped this backwards — a parent minted a code and somebody typed it into the panel — which sent the secret TO the untrusted screen and made a person stand at a hallway touchscreen entering six digits and a label. Corrected on the household's report that it was contrary to how every pairing flow actually works, and they were right for better reasons than convention: the panel now takes NO input at all, and approval happens on a surface where the parent is already signed in.

- **The flow**: open the app URL on the screen. Paired, it loads. Not paired and refused, it shows a six-digit code and polls. A parent types that code in Config → People → Trusted devices (or taps the push, below) and the screen loads its board. It self-heals — a factory-reset panel just needs the URL again, with no admin action first.
- **Asked for, never volunteered.** The pairing screen appears in response to a **401/403**, not on render: a render that POSTs is a bug on its own terms (a kiosk render test caught it immediately), and until enforcement is on an unpaired screen works fine, so demanding pairing would be a visible change nobody asked for.
- **A push to the parents carries the code** (household's idea): `🖥️ A screen wants to join · Code 123456 · asking from this network`, deep-linking to `/app?pair=123456`, where the PWA shows what is asking and takes one tap. The person at the panel is usually the one who cannot walk to a laptop, and a notification you have to act on twice is one people put off. A failed push never stops the screen showing its code — the wall is the fallback and it always works.
- **SHELLS ARE PUBLIC; THE DATA IS NOT.** Forced by this slice and it is now a rule: every HTML page is reachable, every `/api` route is gated. The ways IN are drawn by the shells themselves — the sign-in overlay lives in the admin pages, the pairing screen lives in nav — so gating a page means a refused browser gets a bare 403 with no way to fix it: a panel could never show the code that would let it in, and a parent could never reach the box that would sign them in. The templates carry no household data; every one fetches what it draws. Pinned by `test_auth.scenario_v`.
- **TWO REAL HOLES IN S1 CLOSED HERE**, both the same mistake — treating a header's PRESENCE as proof: `identify()` returned the `device` tier to anyone who sent `X-Device-Token`, and did the same for `X-Service-Token`, which would have made the header its own password. Both now verify against what was actually issued (`storage.get_device_by_token`, `hmac.compare_digest`). Neither was reachable while the guard was dark, but they had to be right *before* the flip rather than at it.
- **`nav.html` carries the device fetch wrapper** so it is in place before any board fetch on every page a panel can draw — guarded for the non-browser case, because nav's script is also executed under node by `test_nav_runtime`.
- Tests: `test_accounts.py` scenarios r–u (a token must be issued not merely sent; a panel cannot reach `/api/settings`, `/api/download_db` or `/config`; the device asks and a parent answers; asking again replaces the old code; an expired request is never approvable).

## Argyle gets a credential (v2.254.0 — auth arc S7)

The HA custom component calls `http://local-chauffeur:8000`, so it has always arrived on the internal hostname with nothing to present — which is why the local-origin grace existed. This is what it presents instead.

- **`POST /api/account/service-token`** (parent-only) mints it, and **shows it in full exactly once**, on Config → People → Argyle. A secret you can never see again is a secret somebody writes on a sticky note; rotating replaces the old one immediately, which is the point of having the button. Merged into settings rather than written through `storage.update_settings` alone — that function truncates and re-inserts the whole row, so handing it one key would wipe every setting the household has.
- **The component sends `X-Service-Token`** and its config flow gained an optional field, validated at setup: a 401/403 comes back as "Chauffeur refused the token — check it was copied in full", so a mistyped paste is answered by the form rather than discovered days later by asking Argyle a question and getting nothing.
- **The grace is a switch, not a law.** `service_local_grace` defaults **on**, and **absent means on** — every install that predates this release has no such key, and defaulting to off would have silenced Argyle in every household the moment the add-on rebuilt. Turn it off once the integration holds its token; the UI says exactly that, and says what leaving it on means (a permanently trusted network, guest phones and smart plugs included).
- Optional token in the component for the same reason: a household mid-migration still has the grace on, and requiring one would take Argyle away before they had one to paste.
- Tests: `test_accounts.py` scenarios v–w (the grace is a switch; absent defaults to on) and `scenario_u` from S6 (a service token must MATCH, not merely be present). The route-classification test caught `/api/account/service-token` unclassified on its first run — working as designed.

## One apostrophe blanked the config page (v2.254.1)

Reported from the box: the config page came up as a row of tabs with nothing underneath. The cause was a single character — `'Replace Argyle's token'` in the S7 rotate button, where the apostrophe closed the string and ended `configApp()`'s entire script.

The failure mode is what makes this worth a test rather than a fix:

- **Silent.** No Python raised, no test failed, the server returned 200. The error existed only in a browser console nobody was looking at.
- **Total.** When an Alpine component fails to initialise, every `x-show` on it evaluates falsey, so one bad character hides the whole page rather than one control.
- **Easy to reintroduce**, because this project writes a great deal of JavaScript inside Jinja, where no editor offers syntax help.

`tests/test_template_js.py` now parses every inline `<script>` in every template with `node --check`, substituting the Jinja away first (`{{ }}` → a literal, `{% %}` → nothing) since the subject is the JavaScript's shape rather than the render. Verified against the broken tree: it fails there and passes here.

## The first-run panel could never appear (v2.255.0)

Two independent bugs, both found on the box, both silent.

**1. `settings` was never a thing.** The S3/S7 panels bound `x-model="settings.smtp_host"` and friends, but `configApp()` keeps flat camelCase properties and has no `settings` object at all — six invented bindings. Alpine threw `ReferenceError: settings is not defined` per control, into a console nobody reads, and the panels rendered as nothing. They now use an `authSettings` object that loads from `/api/settings` and **POSTs only its own keys**, which is the decentralisation rule stated literally.

**2. Supervisor sets `X-Forwarded-For` itself.** `arrived_via_ingress()` disqualified any request that looked forwarded — and supervisor forwards ingress to the add-on with exactly that header, so **every genuine ingress request read as external** and `may_claim` was never true. The discriminator is now Cloudflare's own `CF-Connecting-IP`/`CF-Ray`, which cloudflared stamps on everything it forwards and an outside caller cannot remove; supervisor never sends them. Also widened the identity header to the spellings supervisor actually uses (`X-Remote-User-Id`/`-Name`) and made an absent admin flag permissive, since refusing on its absence makes first-run impossible on exactly the installs that lack it. **Caveat recorded**: behind a plain reverse proxy that sets no CF headers, `X-Ingress-Path` could be forged from outside — this is sound for cloudflared specifically, which is what the household runs.

**`GET /api/account/env`** was added to settle it from evidence rather than from my guesses about header names — the bus arc's "a guessed entity name is the whole feature off", one layer down. It echoes back only the caller's OWN headers plus the computed verdicts, so it says nothing about the household.

**`tests/test_template_js.py` gained the second half of the blank-page guard**: every `x-model` root must be defined somewhere in the template and its includes. The parse check could not see this one — the script was valid, the binding simply named state that did not exist. `x-for` scope names are excluded, since Alpine defines those.

## Two panels, one name (v2.256.0)

Asked from the wall, and correct: the music card called every unnamed panel **"Chauffeur screen"**, so a house with two of them registered two Music Assistant players wearing one name. The audio never actually collided — each browser mints its own `playerId` and the Sendspin relay is per-connection — but everything built on the NAME did, and the symptoms are individually baffling.

- **The generic fallback is gone.** `_tile_music` resolves only the SHARED half of the name: an explicit `screen_name`, then `"{room} screen"`, then **empty**. It could not do better here in any case — the board payload is cached across panels, so a device-specific name minted server-side would be served to the second panel as the first one's. Empty means "the browser must name itself".
- **The browser's ladder is per-device**: the board's answer → **the label a parent gave this device when they paired it** (`GET /api/account/this-device`, open because the caller already knows the id it is asking about, and `named:false` for the defaults "Wall panel"/"A device" — a default label is not an identity) → `"Chauffeur screen {4 chars of the device id}"`. Ugly at the floor and deliberately so: two prettier ways to get "Kitchen screen" come first. The name is read through a GETTER at connect time, so the label landing a moment after the board does is the one that registers.
- **What the card shows is "This Panel"**, never the MA name. Two jobs: the MA name must be unique across a house so a person can pick the right screen out of that list, which makes it exactly the wrong thing to read off the panel you are standing at. Same split the PWA already drew with "This phone".
- **Ambiguity is refused, not guessed at.** `entityIn` used `find`, i.e. the FIRST of several matches — and HA deduplicates the entity_id, not the friendly name, so two "Chauffeur screen" players gave one panel the OTHER one's entity: its now-heart hearted the other room's track and its twin-hide removed the wrong row. Now: id match, then exactly-one exact name, then exactly-one loose name, else `null` with `ambiguous` set, and the cannot-find sentence says which it is. `clashesIn()` puts a plain warning on the card when another MA player is already wearing this screen's name.
- **One device is one player.** `boardLocalPlayers` is keyed by DEVICE, not by card: two music cards on one board were two clients registering with the same stored id, taking turns being kicked by MA. Cards subscribe (`_tiles`) and the last one out stops it. The localStorage slot is `…::screen::{deviceId}` — deliberately NOT name-derived, since a name can change (a room renamed, a label arriving late) and a key that moved with it would orphan the registration MA already has. `identity.legacyKeys` adopts what earlier versions wrote so an upgrade does not leave a dead duplicate.
- **A connection that dies immediately is not a success** — the "(connecting…)" flicker seen once a second on a real wall. `retries` was cleared the instant `connect()` resolved, so a socket that opened and died 200 ms later reset the backoff to 1.5 s and the player sat in a tight loop forever instead of backing off and saying so. The counter now clears only after the connection has HELD for 20 s, and **every** close records code, reason and how long it held (`lastClose` / `closeReason()`), surfaced on the card — a wall panel has no devtools, and "1006 after 0.4s" is the whole diagnosis.
- Tests: `test_music_card.py` (37 scenarios; five new), `test_accounts.scenario_o2`.

## Five admin pages went black (v2.256.1)

Reported after the auth arc: Schedule, Calendar, Trips, Map and Moments showed nothing through ingress but Home Assistant's own chrome. Not an authorization failure at all — the guard is still dark — and the third member of the blank-page family, after the apostrophe (v2.254.1) and the binding to state that never existed (v2.255.0).

S6's pairing overlay (`components/panel_enrol.html`, drawn by nav.html on **every** page) is `fixed inset-0 z-[9500] bg-black`, hidden by `x-cloak`. **`x-cloak` hides nothing on its own**: it needs a `[x-cloak] { display: none }` rule from the host page AND Alpine to strip the attribute afterwards. Seven templates define that rule; the six that do not — calendar, dashboard, map, moments, trips, trip/trip_kiosk — also run **no Alpine at all**, so on exactly those pages the overlay painted over everything, permanently, with HTTP 200 and a clean console.

- **The component carries both halves now**: an inline `style="display:none"` (the one that holds when there is neither a stylesheet rule nor Alpine — `x-show` removes the property outright when it shows, so they do not fight) and its own `[x-cloak]` rule for anything else cloaked under nav.
- **Test**: `test_template_js.scenario_a_cloaked_element_is_hidden_by_something_the_page_actually_has` — any ASSEMBLED page containing `x-cloak` must also contain a rule that hides it. Verified against the shipped markup: it names all nine affected files.
- **KNOWN GAP, deliberately left**: on a page with no Alpine the overlay cannot DRAW either, so a kiosk refused on `/trip?kiosk=true` has no way to show its pairing code. Nothing is lost today (`chfRequestPairing` only fires on a 401/403 and enforcement is off), but **S8 must not flip `auth_enforce` until those pages either run Alpine or send a refused screen somewhere that does.**

## The panel was running last week's JavaScript (v2.256.2)

Reported from the wall the moment v2.256.0 deployed: `MusicLogic.deviceId is not a function`, three times over, on `/music?panel=true&kiosk=true`. The function was in the shipped file. **Nothing under `/static` carried a version**, so the panel kept the `music_logic.js` it had cached and the freshly-rendered page called into it — this week's markup against last week's module, with the fix already on the box.

That failure is silent on the server (HTTP 200, correct bytes on disk), total on the client, and it can happen to any asset here. It is also the one that OUTLIVES a deploy, which makes it worse than the three blank-page bugs before it: rebuilding the add-on does not clear it.

- **`|ver`** (a Jinja filter, `main._versioned`) stamps `?v=<mtime><size>` on every `<script>` and `<link>` under `/static` — 50 references across 19 templates. Keyed on the FILE rather than the release on purpose: stamping with the version would re-pull mapbox-gl, Alpine and the fonts onto every panel at every bump, and this project bumps on every change. mtime+size changes exactly when the file does. A missing file renders unstamped rather than raising — it is a 404 either way, and a cache key must not take a page down.
- Images are deliberately NOT stamped: they are stable, and re-downloading them buys nothing.
- **Test**: `test_template_js.scenario_every_script_and_stylesheet_carries_a_version` — every `src`/`href` naming a `.js` or `.css` under `/static` must go through `|ver`, and `main.py` must register the filter (templates calling an unregistered filter is itself a whole-page Jinja error).

## The party that knew why never said (v2.256.3)

Two field reports from the same session, one shape: at every point where something knew the cause, it dropped it.

- **PWA: "Adopted Websocket closed before opening."** That is sendspin-js naming a symptom. Our own relay had already closed that socket with the actual cause — "Music Assistant Sendspin server not found", or "Could not reach Music Assistant" — and `localPlayer`'s close handler threw it away, because it returned early on `if (!self.active)`. The player had never come up, which is precisely when the reason is the only useful thing there is. It now repeats the relay's words on a pre-open close.
- **Panel: connected, sent the client hello, gone inside a second, no reason.** Preceded in the console by `[Opus] Running in insecure context, falling back to FLAC/PCM`. A page served over plain http is not a secure context, the browser withholds the Opus decoder, and Music Assistant hangs up on a client that cannot offer it. From the room that is a player flickering "(connecting…)" forever, with the diagnosis in a console a wall panel does not have.
  - **`MusicLogic.contextWarning()`** returns that sentence when `isSecureContext === false`. Deliberately NOT a block — some setups may negotiate the FLAC/PCM fallback happily, and refusing to try would remove a working feature to prevent a possible one. It is said ONCE, on the first drop that lasted under the 20 s stability window with no close reason, which is the exact signature; and again in the give-up message.
- **The relay forwards Music Assistant's close frame.** It is the only party that ever sees it — the browser just sees its socket end. `sendspin_relay` now logs `[sendspin] upstream closed <code>: <reason>` and passes the code and reason on to the browser (1005/1006 normalised to 1011, since "no status was sent" is not a status you may send), so the card can print MA's own words.
- Tests: `test_music_card.scenario_a_refusal_is_repeated_rather_than_swallowed`.

## Two doors, two different reasons the music would not play (v2.256.4)

The screen player failed on BOTH routes into this house, for unrelated causes, and the card said the same nothing either way. Naming them apart is the whole fix — they need different boxes touched.

- **Through the Cloudflare tunnel (https):** `WebSocket connection to 'wss://…/api/sendspin/ws' failed` — the HANDSHAKE never completed, so nothing in Chauffeur ever ran. A tunnel or reverse proxy carrying ordinary requests perfectly well while dropping WebSocket upgrades is a default on more of them than it should be. The client now tracks whether the socket ever fired `open`: no reason + never opened is reported as **"could not open its audio connection to `{host}` … whatever sits in front of Chauffeur has to pass WebSocket upgrades"**, naming the host, because "the LAN address works and the tunnel does not" is the sentence that finds this. A handshake that never completes will not complete on the seventh try, so the give-up message says what would have to change instead of inviting another tap.
- **Through Home Assistant ingress (http):** the socket connects, `[Opus] Running in insecure context, falling back to FLAC/PCM`, client hello, gone inside a second. A page on plain http is not a secure context and the browser withholds the Opus decoder.
  - **`contextWarning()` names the ORIGIN, not the route.** Its first draft advised "reach Chauffeur through Home Assistant" and the household read it while doing exactly that — **ingress inherits HA's own scheme**, so an HA served over http hands out insecure pages through every door. Advice that describes a route rather than a requirement sends somebody to check the place they are already standing.
- Both are said ONCE, from the shape of the failure, and neither blocks the attempt: a setup that negotiates the FLAC/PCM fallback happily must not be refused to prevent a failure it does not have.
- Tests: `test_music_card.scenario_a_refusal_is_repeated_rather_than_swallowed`.

## The guard could not be handed a WebSocket (v2.256.5)

`TypeError: _auth_guard() missing 1 required positional argument: 'request'`, from the add-on log, and it is the whole thing. Not the tunnel, which was carrying the upgrade perfectly.

A global FastAPI dependency runs on WEBSOCKET routes too, and FastAPI fills a `Request` parameter only when the connection actually is one:

```python
if dependant.request_param_name and isinstance(request, Request):
elif dependant.websocket_param_name and isinstance(request, WebSocket):
```

A guard asking for `Request` matched neither branch on a websocket, so it was called with no arguments at all and the handshake 500'd. **Every WebSocket connection in the app has failed since S1 (v2.247.0).** There is exactly one WebSocket route — `/api/sendspin/ws` — so the entire visible symptom was that no screen and no phone could ever be a Music Assistant player, on any door into the house.

- **`HTTPConnection`**, the common base of both, is filled unconditionally (`dependant.http_connection_param_name`). The guard takes one of those. A websocket has no method, so the table sees `'WEBSOCKET'` — the audit then says what it saw, and a method-specific rule can never silently capture a handshake.
- **Refusing a handshake needs a close code, not a status code**: the guard raises `WebSocketException(1008)` on a websocket scope. Dark today, but S8 flips it, and this arc's own discipline is that the hole closes before the flip rather than at it.
- **`contextWarning` is now gated on the socket having actually OPENED.** sendspin-js's `connect()` resolves without waiting for the socket, so a handshake the server had already 500'd still set `active` — and the insecure-page warning then blamed a codec for a failure that never reached one. It sent a whole diagnosis to the wrong box. A page can be insecure and that be beside the point; only a connection that opened has an opinion worth printing about what closed it.
- Tests: `test_auth.scenario_the_guard_runs_on_a_websocket_too` pins both the parameter FastAPI will fill and the guard awaited on a real websocket scope.

**The lesson, for the next global dependency**: anything applied to `FastAPI(dependencies=[...])` runs on every protocol the app speaks, and the type it asks for decides whether it can. A test that exercises only HTTP will pass while an entire transport is broken.

## Only a refusal pairing could fix offers pairing (v2.257.0)

Asked from the household, and the right question: *should* a panel be showing pairing requests yet? No — the guard is dark, `check_request` returns None for everything, and an unpaired screen works exactly as it always did. Not seeing one is correct.

But nav's fetch wrapper fired `chfRequestPairing()` on **any** 401/403, and the guard is not the only thing here that returns one. Of the 22 `403` raises in `main.py`, most are domain rules rather than authentication — `"This chore isn't available to you"`, `"{name} isn't on this chore"`, `"Not your routine"`, `"Only children redeem rewards"`, `"You can only check off your own tasks"`, `"Parent authorization required"` — and every one is reachable from an interactive board. A child tapping a sibling's chore on the kitchen wall would be answered with a full-screen six-digit pairing code.

Wrong in kind, not just startling: **pairing could not have fixed any of them.** A trusted device is the `DEVICE` tier; no amount of it makes that chore theirs, or makes the screen a parent. The wall was offering a remedy for a refusal that remedy does not address — and after S8 flips enforcement, real refusals and domain 403s fly around together, so the panel has to tell them apart.

- **The guard signs its own refusals**: `X-Auth-Refusal: <tiers that would have satisfied the rule>`, from `verdict['needs']`. Set by `_auth_guard` and nowhere else, so a domain 403 raised deep in a handler cannot be mistaken for an authorization one.
- **The wrapper keys on `device` being in that list.** A board read refused for want of trust says `device,member,parent` → pairing is the right offer. `/api/settings` says `parent` → no pairing, because a paired screen is still not a parent; a surface seeing `member`/`parent` should be asking somebody to sign in, which is a different screen.
- Tests: `test_auth.scenario_only_a_refusal_pairing_could_fix_offers_pairing` drives the real guard under enforcement for both cases and pins the `'device'` literal in nav.html to `auth.DEVICE`, the same way the music card's sentinel is pinned.

## Every invite this app ever sent went to /api/members/undefined/invite (v2.257.1)

"Member not found" on Send Invite, and it was never anything to do with the SMTP settings that had just been filled in. `sendInvite(member)` read `member.id`; the markup handed it `memberEdit` — the object `startEditMember` builds field by field and deliberately does NOT copy an id into, because the id has a home of its own in `editMemberId`. So the URL was `api/members/undefined/invite`, `get_member('undefined')` returned None, and the endpoint 404'd. **Invites have never worked**, on any release since S3 (v2.249.0).

Valid JavaScript, valid Alpine, a real route, a real object, a 404 — the fifth member of the family that includes the apostrophe (v2.254.1), the phantom `x-model` root (v2.255.0) and the unhidden cloak (v2.256.1).

- **`sendInvite()` takes no argument now**, and that is the fix rather than a tidy-up: it reads `editMemberId` and `memberEdit.email` from the component's own state, where the two cannot disagree, instead of trusting a caller to pass the right object. The button is disabled without an `editMemberId` as well as without an email. The email posted is the one TYPED rather than the one last saved — the server persists whatever it is given, and somebody who just entered an address and pressed Invite means that one.
- **Test: `test_template_js.scenario_an_id_in_a_url_comes_from_something_that_has_one`**, and it follows the whole chain rather than one end of it — markup handler `fn(arg)` → `fn`'s body interpolating `${param.id}` into a template literal → `arg` being a component-state object literal that never gets an id. The first draft of this test only inspected the function body, where `member` is a PARAMETER and therefore unknowable; it passed on the broken code. Verified against HEAD: it names `sendInvite() <- memberEdit` and nothing else.

## One setting with a page on the end broke three kinds of link (v2.257.2)

`{"detail":"Not Found"}` from a freshly mailed invite. The route was fine; the ADDRESS in front of it was not — the link read `https://<host>/app/account/set-password`.

**Public App URL** (`public_base_url`) held the address the family's phones actually open, which is the PWA at `/app`. A fair reading of a field whose help said *"the HTTPS address the family's phones use to open the app"*. But every consumer appends its OWN absolute path, so that single value silently produced:

- `…/app/account/set-password` — invites and password resets, 404
- `…/app/app` — the HA companion notification deep link (the web-push lane was already immune: it goes RELATIVE, which is the same lesson learned once before)

- **`_public_origin()`** drops a trailing path **when it names a page of this app** — the segment is checked against the first path component of every registered route. A path matching no route of ours is kept, because that is a mount prefix and stripping it would break an install served under one. All three consumers go through it.
- **`_account_link` no longer emits a bare path.** With no setting at all it falls back to the origin of the request that minted the link, forwarded scheme and host honoured — a parent issuing an invite is by definition holding a working address, and the old fallback was `''`, which mailed `/account/set-password?token=…` to somebody's phone.
- **`_account_link_warning`** says what is wrong with the address while the PARENT still has it: no origin at all, minted through ingress (whose path token rotates, so the link would rot), or pointing somewhere other than where they are standing. Shown beside the link in the invite box. The next person to notice otherwise is a grandparent reading a 404 with nobody to ask.
- **The wording that invited it is fixed** in both the registry and the field's own help: the domain only, no page, and why.
- Tests: `test_accounts.scenario_an_invite_link_carries_an_address_that_works` covers all five states including the `/app` case and a genuine mount prefix.

## The first thing the app ever shows somebody (v2.258.0)

The set-password page is where an invite lands: a standalone page, no shell, opened in a mail client by a grandparent who may never have heard of Chauffeur. It shipped as a car emoji over two unstyled inputs on a hardcoded near-black — the household called it cheap, and they were right. It is the app's first impression and it looked like a debug form.

- **The app's own wordmark**, markup-identical to nav.html: the blue tile, the lightning glyph, the blue→indigo gradient text. Somebody told "you've been added to the family's Chauffeur" should meet the same mark on the page the link opens. A test pins the SVG path and the gradient against nav's, so a rebrand cannot leave this page behind.
- **Themed by the token layer, not by hand.** It loads `theme.css` before `tailwind-app.css` and uses ordinary utility classes, so `bg-gray-950`/`bg-gray-900`/`text-gray-100` restyle themselves — the light palette INVERTS the neutrals, which is the whole point of the tokens. The one hand-written rule paints `html` before anything loads, so a slow connection never flashes white behind a dark card. Nobody arriving from an email has a stored theme choice, so `prefers-color-scheme` picks it, set before paint.
- **A real card**: bordered surface, one clear heading per state, and four distinct states that each look finished — checking (spinner), expired (amber, and it says what to do next), the form, and done (green tick, "you're signed in on this device").
- **Show/hide on the password**, which is not decoration: a phone keyboard, a password being invented on the spot, and two fields that must agree. Being able to look is what prevents the third attempt.
- **The strength meter fills on LENGTH**, the one rule the server actually enforces — not on a score for symbols, which pushes people toward `Passw0rd!` and away from four words they will remember. The submit button disables below the minimum instead of letting somebody press it and be refused by an endpoint. `_MIN_PASSWORD` is pinned across the Python/template boundary by a test: the number the form states, the number it enforces, and the number the server enforces cannot drift apart.
- Tests: `test_accounts.scenario_the_set_password_page_is_the_first_thing_the_app_ever_shows`.

## Three people were not on the identity screen (v2.258.1)

Reported straight after an invite was accepted: the new account holder was missing from **Select Family Member**, and so were two others — none of it correlated with who had an email, because accounts had nothing to do with it.

The screen draws two lists: the drivers, then "the members who are not one of them". The second was `membersData.filter(m => !m.driver_id)`, and `driversData` drops `is_disabled` rows. **A member linked to a disabled driver was on neither list** — no driver card, and excluded from the member list for having a `driver_id`. They could not sign in as themselves anywhere in the app.

`is_disabled` is a SCHEDULING fact — out of the solver, off the rota — and it had quietly become an identity one. Disabling somebody as a driver deleted them as a person.

- **The test is now "is this person already drawn above?"** (`!drawnDriverIds.has(m.driver_id)`), never "do they have a driver_id". A member whose driver row is disabled or deleted is still a member of this family.
- **The same mistake sat in the restore path.** `restoredPassenger` used the identical `!m.driver_id`, so even a member who could find themselves on the picker was refused on the next load and bounced back to a screen they were not listed on. Both halves of one person disappearing, from one wrong predicate written twice.
- **The Argyle FAB is gone from the identity screen** (household nitpick, and correct): Argyle answers AS somebody, so a chat button before anybody has said who they are cannot work. The rule was inline in `applyViewVisibility`, which that screen never calls, so the button simply stayed wherever the last screen left it. It is `updateAgentFab()` now — one rule, called by both — and it asks the SCREEN rather than `selectedMemberId`, which survives in localStorage and can still name somebody the app just failed to restore, which is exactly the state that lands on the picker.
- Tests: `test_panel_chrome`, two scenarios, both verified to fail against the previous commit.

## Accepting an invite now vouches the phone it happened on (v2.258.2)

Found while verifying the two lockout-recovery paths ahead of S8:

- **Invite → password** is the complete remote rescue: the link page, the peek and the set-password POST are all `ANYONE`-tier on purpose, so they answer while locked out, from anywhere. Spending the link sets the password, verifies the email, kills every other outstanding link and signs the member in on the spot.
- **A PIN only opens trusted ground** (a vouched device, or LAN/ingress) — the auth endpoint refuses an untrusted origin before reading the PIN at all. Parent hand path (clear → set, first-set open) unlocks home surfaces; the invite is the tool for the remote case. A session minted on trusted ground travels afterwards.

The gap: `_trust_this_device` vouches the device on every password sign-in — login, claim, **and invite-accept** — by reading `X-Device-Id`. The standalone set-password page has no nav and no fetch wrapper, so it never sent the header and the vouch silently no-oped: the invite signed somebody in without trusting the phone it happened on, and the day that token died, their PIN could not reopen it. The page now mints/reads the shared `chauffeur_device_id` slot and sends it with the set-password POST. Test pins the header and the slot in the page source.

## An invite finishes the account it started (v2.259.0)

Two gaps in the handoff, both from the next surface assuming somebody arrived by a route they had not taken.

- **No PIN was ever offered to an invited member.** The app offers one inside `ensureMemberAuth`, which returns early when a token for that member is already stored — exactly what the set-password page writes. So the offer was unreachable by anyone who came in by invite. Not a lockout (Decision 9 takes password OR PIN), but it lands them at S8's 90-day token expiry typing a password on a kitchen tablet, which is the friction Decision 4c demoted the PIN to prevent. Offered on the set-password page now, as an optional step after the password: skipping burns the same `chauffeur_pin_offered_{id}` marker `offerPinSetup` uses, so declining once is an answer rather than a question re-asked on the next screen. A member a parent already gave a PIN skips the step. The 4–8 digit rule is pinned to `_valid_pin_format` by a test.
- **An invited DRIVER was sent to the picker.** The page wrote `chauffeur_member_id` but never `chauffeur_driver_id`, and the app only auto-restores a non-driver — so anyone with a driver identity was asked who they were seconds after proving it. A disabled driver id is harmless here: the app finds no matching row and falls through to the member path (v2.258.1).

### Open design question: the member picker should not be the front door

Raised by the household, and it is **Decision 4, already settled and still undone**: "the member-name leak that the picker created is settled by deleting the picker as the front door." S3's slice list says "the sign-in page that replaces the picker" and S3 shipped everything except that. `/api/members` is still `ANYONE`-tier, carrying a comment that says so.

The household's own framing is the right one: the picker is a sign-out/sign-in-as-someone-else flow nobody should be using, it invites impersonation wherever a member has no PIN, and it publishes the family's names to anyone who loads the page. Prettier is not a reason.

The complication that stops it being a deletion: **Decision 4b** — Sprout and Explorer have `own_account: False` and no email by design, so an email+password front door has no room for them. The resolution that fits the machinery already built: a **login page for untrusted origins, the picker only on trusted ground**. A device somebody has vouched for already knows the household; that is where faces-and-a-PIN belongs, and it is exactly what Decision 4c says the PIN is for. `/api/members` then stops answering before authentication off trusted ground, which closes the leak. To be built in S8 alongside the flip.

## The table meets its real callers (v2.260.0 — auth arc S8, part 1)

S8 builds dark, and the first job was correcting what the live audit and a read of the actual callers said the S1 table got wrong — every one of these classified a route for a caller that never makes the request, and would have died at the flip:

- **The Argyle lane was robots-only, and Argyle's users are the family.** The chat bar in `control_center.html` (drawn on panels AND member pages) and the PWA's own bar both POST `/api/chat`; `/api/chat/*` is now `WALL_OR_SERVICE` — anonymous is the only refusal. `/api/v2/chat/stream` (the bar's read side) likewise; `/api/v2/converse` stays robots-only because it is the HA Assist webhook and no browser posts it. `test_auth.scenario_e` moved its "not a member's lane" example accordingly.
- **The music card's HA lanes**: `GET /api/ha/media_players`, `POST /api/ha/media_players/{entity_id}/command` and `GET /api/ha/image64/{encoded}` are carved out `WALL` above the `/api/ha/*` admin prefix (first hit wins). The board's music card lists players, sends transport commands and draws artwork from a wall.
- **`/api/sendspin/ws`** (the app's one WebSocket — the screen player) and **`GET /api/unsplash/background`** (trip backgrounds, drawn by the trip kiosk as CSS urls) both gained `WALL`.
- **The headerless channels now carry the token on the QUERY STRING**, which is why `identify()` has always read `member_token`/`device_token` there: EventSource, WebSocket and `<img>`/CSS urls can set no headers, so the fetch wrappers never touch them, and every such connection was anonymous no matter who was signed in. `chfAuthUrl` (nav.html for the 16 nav pages, a member-only twin in app.html, `authUrl` in music_logic.js) appends member-first-then-device — member first because the server prefers the device tier when both arrive, which would lock a member stream on a shared tablet. Applied to all six `new EventSource(` sites, the sendspin WebSocket, the artwork proxy and all seven unsplash url constructions.
- Tests: `test_auth.scenario_e2` pins every lane and that the carve-outs did not open the prefixes they sit above; `test_template_js.scenario_a_stream_carries_the_token_on_its_query_string` fails on any future `new EventSource(` without `chfAuthUrl` and pins the two music_logic.js channels.

## A session dies of old age, and a stolen phone dies on purpose (v2.261.0 — auth arc S8, part 2)

Decision 8, built: member sessions were immortal — `get_member_by_token` was a bare lookup, so a phone stolen in June was signed in at Christmas.

- **90 days** (`storage.MEMBER_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`), enforced at the lookup so there is exactly one place a token can be believed. Expired means REMOVED, not merely refused — a dead row left behind would come back to life if the TTL were ever raised. The PIN re-opens a trusted device afterwards (Decision 4c), so the common renewal is four digits rather than a password — and v2.259.0's PIN offer on the invite page exists precisely so invite-onboarded members on shared screens hit this gently.
- **Rows with no `created_at` are grandfathered from NOW, written back** — expiring the whole installed base at deploy time would sign every phone out at once, this arc's cardinal sin.
- **"Sign out everywhere"** on the member card (Config → People), parent-gated like `pin/clear` because the person it exists for has just lost the phone they would have pressed it on. Two halves, both needed: `POST /api/members/{id}/signout` ends every session AND un-trusts the PERSONAL devices that member's own sign-ins vouched (`storage.untrust_devices_vouched_by`). Sessions alone would be theatre — the stolen phone is trusted ground the victim's own login created, so their PIN would quietly re-open it minutes later. Off the LAN, the thief now needs the password. Panels (`kind='panel'`) and other members' phones are untouched; home surfaces keep working because the LAN is trusted ground on its own.
- Tests: `test_accounts` scenarios x/x2/x3 (a session dies of old age and is removed; a legacy token is grandfathered, not executed; the vouched-phone half hits the right devices and nothing else).

## The flip becomes a real control, guarded (v2.262.0 — auth arc S8, part 3: Decisions 5-of-9 and 9)

`auth_enforce` was a stored key with no model field, read by `auth.enforcing()` and settable by nobody — deliberate in S1, because a registry entry obliges a hand path and the surface that owns this switch is the one S8 builds. Built:

- **A declared `Settings` field and a registry entry** (`Enforce sign-in`, integrations group), with its control in a new **Enforcement panel on Config → People** — beside the pairing box, the trusted-device list, Argyle's token and the invite sender, because everything on that surface is deciding who may reach the house.
- **The audit report is drawn NEXT TO the switch** (`GET /api/admin/auth_audit` rendered in the panel: would-deny rows worst-first, the claimed/mismatch identity counters, a Refresh and a "start a fresh window" reset). The arc's rule is flip on evidence; evidence remembered from another page is a hunch. An empty report after days of normal life is stated in the UI as exactly what the switch wants to see.
- **Decision 9, enforced at the write**: the settings POST refuses the false→true transition while any active non-system member holds neither a password nor a PIN — HTTP 400 **naming them**, with the fix in the message (Set PIN on their card, or send an invite). Checked on the transition only, so turning enforcement OFF — the emergency lever — can never be blocked by the same rule. The UI posts `auth_enforce` alone so a refusal never takes unrelated edits down with it, reverts the checkbox, and shows the names.
- Tests: `test_accounts.scenario_y` (refusal names the naked member and writes nothing; the same flip succeeds once everyone holds a credential; off is never guarded). `test_settings_registry` now covers the entry like any other setting.

**Before the flip — a wall-panel checklist (recorded 2026-08-20, from a household audit whose would-deny rows were "mostly wall panel activity").** That report is the arc working, not a fault: a panel that has never shown a pairing code has never been refused, and cannot be while enforcement is off. `panelEnrol.init()` is explicit — *"ASKED FOR, never volunteered… until enforcement is on an unpaired screen works perfectly well"* — so `chfRequestPairing` fires only from the nav fetch wrapper on a 401/403. Three things follow, and the first is the one that can strand a screen:
- **Every wall screen's URL must carry `?panel=true` or `?kiosk=true`.** `chfRequestPairing` returns early otherwise (*"a phone browser has a person behind it who can sign in properly"*), so a screen on a bare board URL would be refused at the flip **with no way to draw a pairing code** — a dead end needing a keyboard at the panel. This is a different gap from the v2.264.0 Alpine one, which is closed: Alpine now loads everywhere, but the overlay still declines to *ask* without the param. Walk the house and check the URLs **before** flipping, not after.
- **`service_local_grace` does NOT cover a panel.** An unpaired panel on the LAN resolves to `SERVICE`, and `WALL = {MEMBER, PARENT, DEVICE}` — `SERVICE` is not in it, so `/api/home_board/*` and `/api/panel/*` refuse it anyway. A panel must become a real `DEVICE`; the LAN bypass is not a substitute.
- **The flip is recoverable by design.** `POST /api/account/devices/pair-request` and `GET /api/account/devices/pair-status` are `ANYONE`, and sit ABOVE `(ANY, '/api/account/devices/*', PARENTS)` — first hit wins — so a refused panel can still ask for a code and poll while locked out. The intended sequence is the one the Enforcement panel states: flip, walk the house, approve each code from a phone.

## The picker stops being the front door (v2.263.0 — auth arc S8, part 4: Decision 4 built at last)

Settled 2026-08-15, left undone by S3, raised again by the household at v2.259.0: the member picker published the family's names to anyone who loaded the page, and invited impersonation wherever a member had no PIN. The resolution honours Decision 4b (Sprout/Explorer have no email by design): **email+password on untrusted origins; faces-and-a-PIN only on trusted ground** — which is exactly what Decision 4c already made the PIN for.

- **`_trusted_ground(request)`** (main.py): a vouched device (`X-Device-Id` on the trusted list), the LAN, or HA ingress. Ingress is checked explicitly because supervisor forwards it with `X-Forwarded-For`, which `arrived_via_tunnel` deliberately reads as external — right for failing toward credentials, wrong as the last word on ingress. `member_auth` now uses the same helper, so "where may a PIN be typed" and "where may the picker draw" are one fact.
- **`GET /api/account/ground`** → `{"trusted": bool}`: one boolean about the caller's own standing, open for the same reason as this-device. The PWA asks it to pick its front door.
- **The PWA's login screen** (`#screen-login` in app.html): email + password → `POST /api/account/login`, storing the same handoff the set-password page performs (token, member id, driver id when there is one). The sign-in vouches the device via `X-Device-Id`, so the picker appears there afterwards — the banking-app ladder, ending where Decision 4c starts. Forgot-password posts `/api/account/forgot` and answers identically either way. "Switch person" is now honestly a sign-out flow: on untrusted ground it lands on the login screen, at home it stays the picker.
- **The leak itself**: `GET /api/members` and `GET /api/drivers` (fetched by every PWA boot AND the pre-auth picker) stay `ANYONE` in the table — the tier table cannot express "trusted ground" — and are gated in the handler by `_gate_family_listing`: any resolved tier answers, anonymous-on-trusted-ground answers, anonymous-off-it gets 401 once enforcing (`X-Auth-Refusal: member,parent`, so nav offers sign-in rather than pairing) and is recorded (`untrusted-members`/`untrusted-drivers`) while dark. Driver **writes** stay parent-only under the `/api/drivers/*` prefix.
- Tests: `test_accounts.scenario_z` (anonymous internet refused on both listings under enforcement; LAN, vouched device and member token all still answer; dark records; ground probe says which door; the GET carve-out did not open writes).

## Every page can draw its own way in (v2.264.0 — auth arc S8, part 5)

The pairing-overlay gap recorded at v2.256.1, closed. Seven templates — calendar, trips, map, moments, trip, trip_kiosk, dashboard — ran no Alpine, so the Alpine components their includes brought in rendered as nothing: a kiosk refused on `/trip?kiosk=true` could never draw its pairing code, and **the S4 sign-in gate on the dashboard was inert from the day it shipped** — at the flip, the dashboard would have 401'd forever with no way to sign in. (The `?panel=true` forms of calendar/map/moments/trips route to home.html and were fine; the `?kiosk=true` forms and both trip pages were not.)

- All seven now load `static/vendor/alpine.min.js`, which activates exactly the two shared components: the pairing overlay everywhere, and the admin gate on the dashboard (bringing it to parity with config, which always had Alpine). Their own scripts stay plain JS.
- **The generic rule is pinned**, not the seven names: `test_template_js.scenario_a_page_carrying_alpine_components_loads_alpine` fails any assembled page whose markup binds `x-data` without loading Alpine — the sixth member of the blank-page family, caught structurally.
- `panel_enrol.html`'s KNOWN GAP comment is retired.

## CORS off `*` (v2.265.0 — auth arc S8, part 6)

The old middleware was `allow_origins=["*"]` **with credentials**, which Starlette honours by echoing whatever Origin arrives — any website could script this API with the visitor's tokens attached. Removed outright rather than narrowed: every browser surface is served by this app and fetches relative URLs (same-origin needs no CORS), the HA component calls server-side where CORS does not apply, and HA card assets are proxied through this origin precisely so the question never comes up. A future native wrapper (Capacitor's `capacitor://localhost`) is a genuine foreign origin and gets a deliberate allowlist when it ships. Pinned by `test_auth.scenario_e3`.

## The invite ends on the home screen (v2.266.0 — install nudge)

An invite necessarily lands in a **browser tab** — a mail link cannot open an app that is not installed — so the onboarding flow ended one step short: account, PIN, and then a new member left living in Safari, where **iOS delivers no web push at all**, meaning no family notifications. The set-password page now hands off with `../app?from=invite`, and the app offers the last step.

- **A bottom sheet, not an overlay, on purpose**: a browser tab is a legitimate way to use the app (a laptop check, a deliberate tab on the kitchen tablet), so the nudge must never take the page hostage. "Not now" snoozes it 30 days; the `?from=invite` arrival bypasses the snooze because there it IS the flow's last step, and the general case additionally requires a signed-in member so it never sits over the login screen or picker.
- **Platform mechanics**: Android stashes `beforeinstallprompt` and shows a real Install button — that event fires only when installable AND not yet installed, so it is the capability check and the don't-nag signal in one. iOS has no API: numbered Share → Add to Home Screen steps, with the share glyph drawn inline. Desktop gets nothing.
- **The guards are the feature**, each pinned by `test_accounts.scenario_z2`: never when already running standalone (`display-mode: standalone` + `navigator.standalone`), never in the HA companion webview (it cannot Add-to-Home-Screen), never via an ingress path (installing one bakes supervisor's rotating token into the icon — the same link rot v2.257.2 fixed in mailed invites), and `appinstalled`/an accepted prompt retires it permanently.

## The nudge that never showed (v2.267.0)

Reported from the box: no sheet. Three causes, one real and two design calls that read as broken:

- **The real one: only the signed-in path ever offered it.** init()'s no-restore branch returned before the offer ran — and the natural test is exactly that branch: a phone browser tab with NO stored sign-in (iOS 17+ gives Safari tabs and the home-screen app separate storage, so even an installed household lands here), shown the picker and nothing else. The flags are now read before the restore branch and the no-restore path offers after `showDriverSelection()` settles — so the sheet rides the picker, but still never the login screen (that screen has the floor).
- **Desktop was mute even where install exists.** Chrome/Edge on desktop fire `beforeinstallprompt` too; a captured prompt now outranks platform sniffing and shows the Install button anywhere it exists. Without one, iOS remains the only platform whose manual steps are worth teaching (Android/desktop without a prompt means the browser cannot install — instructions would dead-end).
- **No way to verify on a device.** `?install=1` now forces the sheet past every guard except standalone (an installed app must never be told to install itself, even in a test), falling back to the iOS steps so something always draws; every silent decline logs its reason via `console.debug('[install-nudge] …')`.

Both new behaviours pinned in `test_accounts.scenario_z2` (the picker path's offer, the verification lever).

## The ride reports itself (v2.268.0 — the ride-status slice)

The diagnosis, from the household: drivers navigate in Apple/Google Maps, so the app is closed for the whole drive — "keep the app open" is not a designable behaviour. The design inverts it: **use the taps you already get** (Start Drive, a push), and make each one carry the most information possible. First feature where the app reads location itself — single foreground fixes at explicit taps, never `watchPosition`, never background.

- **ETA at the Start tap.** `POST /api/drive_status` accepts an optional client fix (bounded 3.5 s, best-effort, `getPositionFix` in app.html); `drive_arrival.eta_for_start` prices the drive from the fix via one Directions call, else from the solver's own edge minutes (free). Stored on the drive-status row (`storage.mark_drive_status` now MERGES extra fields; `get_drive_status`/`get_drive_status_rows` added).
- **The on-the-way push grew a time and an audience.** K2's kid push body becomes "Swim Practice · arriving about 3:58 pm" when an ETA exists (no ETA = unchanged wording — no-guess silence); the same start now tells the PARENTS ("🚗 Dad is driving to Swim Practice" / "Addison · arriving about 3:58 pm"), minus the driver, own once-per-day marker, kid-quiet-hours gate shared. `_clock_label` honours `time_format_24h`.
- **The check-in nudge** (`drive_arrival.run_nudges`, in the 30 s push loop after the passive sweep): an in-progress leg past its ETA (+3 min grace) pushes its driver once — "Arrived at Guitar?" — deep-linking `/app?arrival=<leg>`. Legs >3 h past ETA burn the marker silently; HA-tracked drivers rarely see it because the passive sweep completes their legs first.
- **The tap IS the confirmation** (`drive_arrival.tap_check`, `POST /api/drive_status/arrival`): opening the deep link takes a fix and answers with a fact — within 300 m (`TAP_RADIUS_M`, deliberately looser than the passive sweep's 175 m: the driver has said "I think I'm done" and a school car park is a long way from the pin) the leg completes and the driver sees "✅ checked off", never a question. Verifiably elsewhere → a fresh ETA is computed and **PARKED** (`pending_eta_ts`); no usable fix/pin → the human decides. The already-completed case reads as success, not error.
- **Sharing a new time is the driver's own act** (`POST /api/drive_status/share_eta`): promotes the parked ETA, re-arms the nudge for it, fans out "🚗 New time from Dad" to the same audience. The app never narrates somebody's lateness uninvited — and "not at the destination" is offered alongside "I've arrived" in the choice sheet, because the driver who dropped off and drove on taps from the supermarket.
- **Next-open reconciliation** (`reconcileStaleDrives`, app.html): a leg of the SELECTED driver's still in_progress 2 h past its event gets one question per app open ("Still driving to Guitar?"), which is the catch-all for the push nobody tapped.
- Tests: `test_drive_arrival` +8 scenarios (edge pricing, fix upgrade, tap complete merges-not-replaces, parked ETA untouched until shared, evidence-free tap asks the human, sweep-beat-the-tap is success, nudge once/grace/silent expiry); `test_kid_pushes` +2 (ETA in both bodies, share flow + 404) and the parent fan-out assertions.
- **The native-app story this sets up**: with a background geofence the whole loop — start, drive, arrive, complete — needs no second tap at all. That upgrade slots into `tap_check`/`check_arrivals` unchanged.

## A kid in the back seat is not "on the way" (v2.269.0)

The household's correction of v2.268.0, within a day of shipping it: driving to swim practice FROM HOME, the kids are in the car — "🚗 Dad is on the way!" delivered to the back seat is the push teaching the family the push means nothing. The on-the-way push matters exactly when the car is driving TOWARD the kid.

- **`_leg_is_toward_kids(leg_id)`**: `init_*_1` (the drive TO a pickup waypoint — `_2` is the kid aboard, onward) or any leg whose event is a `_pickup` slice. Everything else — plain home→event, `final_` home, unknowable legs — counts as CARRYING: a wrong silence costs one push, a wrong push devalues them all. Kids hear only toward-legs; **parents hear either way** ("the ride left" is the status they asked for), same dedup markers. The same gate applies to the new-time push.
- **Split-slice lookup fixed**: a `swim_pickup` slice may not exist as its own row in the events cache, and the exact-match lookup meant the pickup drive — the push that matters most — silently sent nothing. `_ride_event` falls back to the base event (as every leg helper already does) and titles it "Pick-up from Swim Practice", because "Swim Practice · arriving about 5:02" reads as the wrong direction to a kid waiting to come home. Assignments fall back variant→base the same way.
- The agent's `start_route` now passes its leg so the gate can decide for voice-started drives too.
- **Recorded, not solved** (roadmap → open design questions): the driver who drops off and leaves WITHOUT the event being split. No return leg exists, so no tap, no ETA, no push — and the kid's situation is real either way. Candidate shapes noted: day-of retro-split at the arrival check-in ("staying?"), a stays/leaves flag on the assignment, or background location (the native track), which dissolves the question without modeling intent and is the strongest single argument for that track.
- Tests: `test_kid_pushes` — kid-in-the-car is parent-only (and a leg the gate cannot read counts as carrying), the pickup slice reaches the waiting kid through the base-event fallback with the direction in the title.

## Not staying? The retro-split (v2.270.0)

Closes the open design question v2.269.0 recorded, on the household's own framing — the spec in one sentence: *"we have all of these systems in place but they don't always get used the way they are built, so we provide other ways for people to opt in in real time."* Events already split three ways at solve time (`#dropoff`/`#pickup` hashtags, attendance rules, the ≥2-hour default) — but the family's real calendar has 45-min–1.5-hr events where the driver drops off and leaves (waits at home five minutes away, improvises a grocery run), and nobody pre-plans those. **An option, never a prompt**: no question is ever forced at drive completion.

- **`POST /api/events/{id}/attendance`** `{action: 'split'|'stay'}` — a day-of, instance-scoped attendance override, stored in app_state with a 48-hour TTL (a Tuesday declaration must never quietly reshape next Tuesday's recurrence). `_attendance_decision` gives it top precedence in the solve: the person in the car outranks the rule written last month, which outranks the 2-hour default. Then the normal background re-solve runs and the pickup slice materializes with real legs — which means everything from this week rides for free: Start tap, ETA, the toward-the-kid "Pick-up from…" push, the arrival check-in.
- **Declaring 'split' PINS both slices to the driver already on the event** (manual overrides, `source: 'retro_split'`) so a mid-day re-solve cannot hand the afternoon to somebody else as a side effect of one honest declaration. Ghost drivers are never pinned — a ghost is a gap, and pinning one would freeze it. `'stay'` (the undo) removes only its own slice pins, never a manual override somebody placed on the base event.
- **Drive history survives the rename** (`_mirror_drive_rows`): the re-solve turns `init_art` into `init_art_dropoff`, and status rows key on leg ids — without mirroring, the drive the driver JUST finished would draw as never-driven and the arrival machinery would lose its ETA mid-flight. Rows are copied with their fields, never moved (the old schedule may still be on a screen for one more poll), and mirror back on the undo.
- **The UI is two real buttons on the drive action sheet** ("Not Staying — Schedule Pick-up" / "Staying — Cancel Pick-up", amber-bordered in the house button style with flat stroke icons — corner-return and undo arrows, no emoji), placed in the order a driver would use them: Start Drive, Mark as Completed, then these, with Cancel separate at the bottom; the mid-drive maps state carries the same pair in the same position (v2.270.1, per the household's review — the first cut was bare text sitting below Cancel, and consistency is king). Drawn only where they mean something: an inbound leg of the SELECTED driver's own event — unsplit offers the split, already-split offers the undo, `final_` legs and other people's drives offer nothing. Reachable from any leg pill, including completed ones, which covers the realized-at-3pm-from-the-couch case. The declared window also becomes genuinely free in the solve, which is exactly where the errand scheduler already looks — "I'm running an errand" needed no new concept.
- **A driver marked as ATTENDING is a stay signal too** (v2.356.0), ranked below the explicit split signals and above the 2-hour default; and the **Attendance Mode dropdown** on both event editors is finally read. See "A drive round the corner is still a drive" for the full ladder.
- Tests: `tests/test_attendance_override.py` (10 scenarios: precedence both directions, attendance in the ladder, the phantom block gone end to end, an explicit split still winning, the dropdown actually read, self-expiry, pins + history mirroring, undo removes only its own pins, ghost never pinned, 404/400).

## A card that goes looking, not told (v2.359.0, superseded by the pool in v2.360.0)

Reported against two of the household's own cards (`custom:ai-media-router-card`
and `custom:ai-media-matrix-card`): both DISPLAYED, and every part of them that
lists speakers or TVs was empty. Nothing errored, because nothing was wrong
with the cards.

`ha_cards.entity_ids()` walks a card's config and ships exactly the entities it
NAMES as `hass.states`. That is right for every card that is told what to show
and wrong for one that DISCOVERS — the matrix card builds its cast list with
`Object.values(hass.states).filter(s => s.entity_id.startsWith('media_player.')
&& !s.entity_id.startsWith('media_player.ai_media_'))`, and was enumerating an
empty house:

| card | ids in YAML | states sent | device list |
|---|---|---|---|
| router (`layout: auto`) | none | **0** | empty |
| matrix | 1 room | **1**, and the filter excludes that prefix | empty |

- **"Also send these entities"** on the Card tile (`entities`): ids and whole
  domains (`media_player.*`), resolved against live states by
  `ha_cards.expand_patterns`. Opt-in, because everything named travels on every
  board refresh. A plain id that matches nothing is NOT dropped — it reaches
  `missing`, where the tile names it, because swallowing a typo is how somebody
  spends an evening wondering why one device never appears.
- **A card sent zero entities now says so** (`note`, drawn under the tile). An
  empty device list is indistinguishable from a working card in a house with no
  devices, and nothing else on the tile would ever tell the household which one
  they are looking at.
- Tests: `test_ha_cards` +7, including both real card shapes and a reproduction
  of the actual cast-list filter.

**Why the slice exists at all, measured** (the old comment claimed "several
hundred kilobytes" without ever checking): 25 media players with realistic
attribute bags is **29.5 KB of JSON, which gzips to 1.0 KB**. The cost is not
the states — it is that the board POLLS (once a minute), re-sending the whole
slice unchanged every tick, embedded PER TILE, with **no compression anywhere
in the app** (`main.py` installs no middleware at all). Home Assistant pays for
the same data once per page load over a WebSocket and then ships only
`state_changed` deltas, with every card on the dashboard sharing one `hass`
object by reference. Ours is a polling cost, not a payload cost. See the
open note below.

## The whole house, once per board, compressed (v2.360.0)

The v2.359.0 "Also send these entities" box worked and put the burden of
knowing a card's internals on the person pasting YAML. The household asked for
a solution that needs no such knowledge, and measurement said it was
affordable, so the box is RETIRED (option, parser and sent-no-entities note
all removed — `test_ha_cards` pins the removal so a partial revert cannot
bring back half of it). Two mechanisms replace it:

**1. The shared state pool.** `ha_cards.states_all()` — every entity in the
house, shaped exactly like `states_for` rows (one `_shape`, so the two can
never drift) — attached ONCE per board payload as `ha_states`, and only when
the board actually hosts a custom card (host-mode tile, or a native stack
carrying host cells). `home.html` hands it to the host
(`ChauffeurHaCards.setStates`) before each `syncCards`, and `makeHass` merges
it UNDER each card's own named states — named rows win a collision, because
they are what `missing` was computed against. A discovering card now walks a
full house; per-tile `states` stays the named slice, so the amber
"not in Home Assistant" warning still names a config typo the pool cannot
contain. Boards with no custom card pay nothing.

**2. Selective gzip, app-wide** (`services/http_compress.py`, installed in
`main.py`). The app had NO compression anywhere; 29.5 KB of state JSON gzips
to 1.0 KB. Starlette's `GZipMiddleware` was deliberately NOT used: it
compresses streaming responses, and gzip buffering a live SSE stream is a
messaging outage. The rule here is structural, not an allowlist — a
single-shot response (one body frame: every JSONResponse and rendered
template) compresses when the client accepts gzip, the content-type is texty
and the body clears 500 bytes; anything sending more than one frame (SSE,
ndjson, FileResponse chunks — so static files too, which are versioned and
browser-cached anyway) passes through untouched by construction. Correct
`Content-Length` recomputation, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, no double-encoding.

Worth stating: when a custom card is on a board, that board's payload now
carries the whole house's states to whoever can view it. The framed dashboard
tile always exposed at least as much, and putting a custom card on a wall is
the household's own act — but it is a wider slice than the named-ids default,
and it travels only on boards that made that choice.

Tests: `test_ha_cards` (pool shape, discovery end to end against the real
cast-list filter, typo still named, the three-part hand path, the box's
removal), `test_ha_card_host_runtime` (the merge in real JS under node —
pool under named states), `test_http_compress` (6 scenarios: fat JSON
shrinks round-trippably, an event stream is never buffered or altered,
no-gzip clients and small/binary/pre-encoded bodies untouched, and the
middleware is actually installed).

## A drive round the corner is still a drive (v2.356.0–v2.358.0)

Three defects, all reported as one sentence from the household: *"I mark the
driver as attending in the event config. That assigns the event to that driver
